basin relief divided by basin length
basin area divided by the square of basin length
number of stream segments divided by basin area
cards.e: Form factor = area / length squared; low values mean a long narrow basin. The other options are drainage density, stream frequency and relief ratio.

cards.q: A drainage basin has a hypsometric integral of about 0.8. This suggests that the basin is
o: youthful, with most of its rock mass not yet eroded
cards.e: The integral is the fraction of the original mass still present. Values above about 0.6 mean a young, little-eroded basin; low values (below about 0.35) mean old age.

cards.q: In a meandering stream, placer gold is most likely to be concentrated
o: in the gravels on the inner side of bends, close to bedrock
on top of the natural levees
on the eroding outer bank of bends
in the clays of the backswamp
cards.e: Heavy grains settle where the current slows, on the inside of bends, and work down to bedrock. The outer bank has the fastest flow and is being eroded, not deposited.

cards.q: The beach sands of Chavara in Kollam district are mined mainly for
cards.e: Chavara is a beach placer of titanium minerals (ilmenite, rutile) with zircon, monazite and sillimanite. Kerala has no beach deposits of gold, tin or diamond.

cards.q: In a granite-gneiss terrain, which geomorphic unit is the best target for a bore well?
o: Bare rocky pediment at the hill foot
Valley fill along a fracture lineament
cards.e: Valley fill stores water in thick loose material, and the fracture below lets water move into the well. Hills and bare rock surfaces shed rain as run-off and store very little.

cards.q: The Survey of India toposheet numbered 58 D/14 is on a scale of
cards.e: 58 is the million sheet, 58 D is the degree sheet at 1:250,000, and 58 D/14 is a 15-minute sheet at 1:50,000. A 1:25,000 sheet needs a further part such as NE.

cards.q: Two villages are 6 cm apart on a 1:50,000 toposheet. The ground distance between them is
cards.e: On 1:50,000, 1 cm = 500 m, so 6 cm = 3000 m = 3 km. Multiplying by 2 instead of dividing gives the wrong 12 km.

cards.q: Where contours cross a stream valley, the V-shape of the contours points
o: toward the nearest ridge crest on the left bank
cards.e: The valley floor is lower than its sides, so each contour bends up-valley to stay at the same height. On a spur the V points downhill instead.

cards.q: On a 1:50,000 map with a contour interval of 20 m, two neighbouring contours are 1 cm apart. The average gradient between them is
cards.e: 1 cm on the map = 500 m on the ground. Gradient = rise / horizontal distance = 20 / 500 = 1 in 25.

cards.q: Open Series Maps of the Survey of India are based on
o: Everest datum and Lambert conformal conic projection
cards.e: Open Series Maps (National Map Policy 2005) use WGS-84 with UTM so that they match GPS. Everest datum with polyconic projection was the system of the older toposheets.

cards.q: On a Survey of India toposheet, contour lines are printed in
cards.e: Brown is used for contours and other relief features. Blue is for water, green for forest and red for settlements and roads.

cards.q: The Palghat Gap in the Western Ghats lies between the
cards.e: The gap, about 30 km wide, has the Nilgiris to its north and the Anamalai Hills to its south. The break between the Cardamom Hills and Agasthyamalai is the much smaller Shencottah gap.

cards.q: 'Chakara' on the Kerala coast refers to
o: sand bars that close river mouths in summer
calm near-shore mudbanks that appear during the south-west monsoon
black heavy-mineral sand streaks on beaches
strong rip currents near harbour mouths
cards.e: Mudbanks are patches of thick fluid mud that damp the waves, so the sea is calm and fish gather there. Black sand streaks are heavy-mineral placers, as at Chavara, and are a different feature.

cards.q: The highest peak in India south of the Himalaya is
cards.e: Anamudi (2695 m) is in Idukki district, Kerala. Doddabetta (2637 m), the highest peak of the Nilgiris, is the tempting wrong choice, but it is lower.

cards.q: A drainage basin has an area of 50 sq km and a basin length of 10 km. Its Horton form factor is
cards.e: Form factor = area / (basin length squared) = 50 / 100 = 0.5. Dividing area by length alone gives 5, which is wrong.

cards.q: In a massive granite terrain, main streams and tributaries make sharp right-angled bends and join at right angles. This rectangular pattern is controlled by
o: a cover of loose glacial deposits
alternating hard and soft sedimentary beds
cards.e: Streams follow fracture lines because broken rock is easy to erode, and two fracture sets at right angles give a rectangular pattern. Alternating beds give trellis drainage, but massive granite has no bedding.

cards.q: Radial drainage is typical of
o: a structural basin or crater floor
a volcanic cone or structural dome
cards.e: Streams flow outward in all directions from a high central point. Flow inward into a basin is the opposite pattern, called centripetal.

cards.q: Which one of the following is NOT an erosional landform of glaciers?
cards.e: An esker is a ridge of sand and gravel deposited by a meltwater stream under the ice. Cirque, arete and roche moutonnee are all cut into bedrock by ice.

cards.q: A medial moraine is formed
o: where a glacier pauses during its retreat
under the ice as a thin sheet of till
where two valley glaciers join and their lateral moraines merge
at the snout of a glacier at its farthest advance
cards.e: The inner lateral moraines of two joining glaciers combine into one dark stripe down the middle. The snout ridge is a terminal moraine, and the pause ridge is a recessional moraine.

cards.q: Varnes's classification of slope movements is based on
o: depth of the failure surface and rock age
speed and volume of the moving mass
type of movement and type of material
cards.e: Varnes (1978) joins a movement type (fall, topple, slide, spread, flow) with a material type (rock, debris, earth), for example 'debris flow'. Speed is used only as an extra description.

cards.q: Which soil group covers the largest area in India?
cards.e: Alluvial soil covers the northern plains, the deltas and the coastal strips. Red and black soils come next but each covers much less area.

cards.q: How many 1:50,000 toposheets make up one 1:250,000 degree sheet of the Survey of India?
cards.e: A 1 degree by 1 degree sheet is cut into 4 x 4 = 16 sheets of 15 minutes each. 256 is the number of 1:50,000 sheets in a whole 4-degree (million) sheet.

cards.q: Which statement about contours is correct?
o: Contours of different value often cross on gentle slopes
Widely spaced contours show a steep slope
Contour V's point downstream where they cross a valley
Evenly spaced contours show a uniform slope
cards.e: Equal spacing means the ground rises by the same amount over the same distance. Wide spacing means a gentle slope, V's point upstream, and contours of different value do not cross.

cards.q: Orthoclase feldspar is changed into kaolinite chiefly by the process of
cards.e: In hydrolysis, hydrogen ions from water replace potassium in the feldspar and clay is left. Hydration only adds whole water molecules to a mineral, as when anhydrite turns to gypsum.

cards.q: Groynes are built at right angles to a beach mainly to
o: trap sand moved by longshore drift
stop sea water entering the groundwater
cards.e: Longshore drift carries sand along the shore, and a groyne catches it on its updrift side to widen the beach. Offshore breakwaters are the structures meant to break waves.

cards.q: According to Darwin's subsidence theory, coral reefs around a sinking volcanic island develop in the order
cards.e: The reef first fringes the island, then a lagoon opens as the island sinks (barrier reef), and at last only a ring of reef is left (atoll).

cards.q: An elbow-shaped bend, a dry wind gap and a misfit stream in a wide valley together point to
cards.e: A headward-cutting stream has diverted the upper part of another river. The beheaded river is left too small for its valley, and its old course is the wind gap. Rejuvenation gives terraces and knickpoints instead.

cards.q: The ultimate base level for the erosion of rivers is
o: the level of the nearest lake
cards.e: A river cannot cut below the level of the sea it enters. A lake is only a local, temporary base level for the stretch of river above it.

cards.q: Stalactites and stalagmites are deposited in limestone caves mainly because the dripping water
o: loses carbon dioxide to the cave air
becomes more acidic in the cave
cards.e: When CO2 escapes, the water can hold less calcium bicarbonate, so calcite comes out. More acid water would dissolve calcite, not deposit it.

cards.q: In which region of Kerala is rice grown on reclaimed land lying below mean sea level?
cards.e: Kuttanad, at the southern end of Vembanad lake, is reclaimed backwater bed kept dry by bunds. The other three regions lie well above sea level.

cards.q: Other things being equal, which drainage basin will give the sharpest and highest flood peak?
o: An elongated basin with low drainage density
A nearly circular basin with low drainage density
A nearly circular basin with high drainage density
An elongated basin with high drainage density
cards.e: High drainage density means fast run-off, and a circular shape means water from all parts arrives together. An elongated basin spreads the flow over a longer time and flattens the peak.

cards.q: A valley with a U-shaped cross-section, truncated spurs and tributary valleys hanging high on its walls was shaped by
cards.e: A glacier fills the whole valley and grinds its floor and sides, cutting off the spurs. A youthful river cuts only its bed, so it makes a V-shaped valley with interlocking spurs.

cards.q: A stony desert plain covered with a sheet of gravel is called
cards.e: Reg is a gravel-covered plain left after wind has removed the sand. Erg is a sand sea and hamada is a bare rock plateau.

cards.q: Rounded boulders wrapped in onion-like concentric shells, seen in jointed dolerite and basalt, are formed by
cards.e: Chemical weathering works inward from the joints and attacks corners fastest, so square blocks become round with loose shells. Frost wedging gives sharp angular fragments instead.

cards.q: Residual bauxite deposits are most likely to be found
cards.e: Bauxite needs long, deep tropical weathering on stable, well-drained flat ground, so it caps old plateau surfaces. Flood plains and steep slopes are too young or erode too fast.

cards.q: Which of these Survey of India sheet numbers denotes a map on 1:250,000 scale?
cards.e: A number with one letter is a degree sheet at 1:250,000. 58 alone is the 1:1,000,000 sheet, 58 D/14 is 1:50,000 and 58 D/14/NE is 1:25,000.

cards.q: A flat desert basin floor that holds a shallow salt lake for a short time after rain is a
cards.e: Run-off collects in the lowest part of a closed basin and evaporates, leaving clay and salt. The bajada is the sloping apron of fans above the playa.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Which wavelength region is the main atmospheric window used to sense heat emitted by the Earth's surface at normal temperatures?
cards.e: The Earth at about 300 K emits most strongly near 10 µm, inside the 8-14 µm window. The 5-8 µm region is blocked by water vapour, and 0.4-0.7 µm is reflected sunlight, not emitted heat.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: The blue colour of the sky and the bluish haze on high-altitude aerial photographs are caused mainly by
cards.e: Rayleigh scattering by gas molecules is far stronger for short (blue) wavelengths. Mie scattering is by dust and smoke of about the same size as the wavelength and affects longer wavelengths too.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: The very high near-infrared reflectance of a healthy green leaf is mainly due to
o: internal cell structure of the leaf
cards.e: Near-infrared light is scattered strongly by the spongy cell structure inside the leaf. Chlorophyll controls the visible bands, where it absorbs blue and red light.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: On a standard false colour composite (FCC), dense healthy vegetation appears
cards.e: In a standard FCC the near-infrared band is shown in red, and vegetation reflects near-infrared strongly. Green is its colour only on a true colour image.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Which band-to-colour assignment gives a standard false colour composite?
o: NIR as red, red as green, green as blue
Red as red, green as green, blue as blue
NIR as blue, red as green, green as red
Green as red, NIR as green, red as blue
cards.e: Each band is shifted one step: near-infrared to red, red to green, green to blue. Red-green-blue shown in their own colours is a true (natural) colour composite.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: On a near-infrared image, a deep clear-water reservoir appears
cards.e: Clear water absorbs nearly all near-infrared energy, so almost nothing returns to the sensor. Bright tones in this band are typical of vegetation, not water.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: A vertical aerial photograph is taken with a camera of focal length 150 mm from 3000 m above flat ground. The photo scale is
cards.e: Scale = f / H = 0.15 m / 3000 m = 1/20,000. The value 1:45,000 comes from wrongly multiplying 150 by 3000 without converting units.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: An aircraft flies at 3500 m above mean sea level over terrain at 500 m elevation, using a camera of 100 mm focal length. The photo scale is
cards.e: Scale = f / (H - h) = 0.1 / (3500 - 500) = 1/30,000. Using 3500 m without subtracting the ground elevation gives the wrong 1:35,000.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: On a vertical photo taken from 2000 m above the base of a tower, the top of a 100 m high tower lies 80 mm from the photo centre. The relief displacement of the tower is
cards.e: d = r x h / H = 80 mm x 100 / 2000 = 4 mm. Units of h and H cancel, so d comes out in the unit of r.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: The image of a chimney on a vertical photo is 5 mm long (base to top), and its top is 100 mm from the principal point. If the flying height above the base is 1500 m, the chimney height is
cards.e: h = d x H / r = 5 x 1500 / 100 = 75 m. This is the relief displacement formula rearranged; the radial distance is measured to the top of the object.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: Which statement about relief displacement on a vertical aerial photograph is correct?
o: It increases as flying height increases
It is greatest at the nadir point
It shifts hilltops towards the photo centre
It is radial from the nadir and zero at the nadir
cards.e: Displacement is radial from the nadir, outward for high points, and nothing at the nadir itself. A higher flying height reduces it, since d = r h / H.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: Flying height is 2000 m above ground. On a stereo pair, the absolute parallax at the base of a hill is 98 mm and the parallax difference between its top and base is 2 mm. The height of the hill is about
cards.e: h = H x dP / (Pb + dP) = 2000 x 2 / (98 + 2) = 40 m. A larger parallax difference would mean a taller hill.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: The usual forward overlap between successive aerial photographs taken for stereoscopic study is about
cards.e: About 60% forward overlap ensures every point appears on two photos. About 20-30% is the side lap between adjacent flight strips, which is the tempting wrong choice.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: An aerial photograph in which the horizon is visible is called a
cards.e: High oblique photos are tilted so much that the horizon appears. A low oblique is tilted but does not show the horizon.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: An aerial photograph differs from a topographic map because the photograph is a
cards.e: All light rays pass through the camera lens, giving a central (perspective) view with relief displacement. A map is orthographic, with every point seen from directly above.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: Which one of the following is NOT a recognition element of visual image interpretation?
cards.e: Tone, texture and association are standard interpretation elements, along with shape, size, pattern, shadow and site. Parallax is a measurement used to find heights from stereo pairs.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: The instrument used with a stereoscope to measure the difference in parallax between two points on a stereo pair is the
cards.e: A parallax bar (stereometer) uses a floating mark to measure parallax difference, which is then converted to height. A planimeter measures area on a map.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: A 23 cm x 23 cm vertical aerial photograph at a scale of 1:20,000 covers a ground area of side
cards.e: Ground distance = photo distance x scale number = 0.23 m x 20,000 = 4600 m = 4.6 km. So one photo covers about 21 square km.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: A sensor with 10-bit radiometric resolution can record how many grey levels?
cards.e: Grey levels = 2 to the power of the bit number, and 2^10 = 1024. The value 256 belongs to 8-bit data.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: The main advantage of a sun-synchronous orbit for earth-resource satellites is that the satellite
o: views the whole Earth disc in one image
passes over a place at the same local solar time each visit
stays fixed over one point on the equator
cards.e: Same local time gives similar sun angle on every image, so scenes of different dates are comparable. Staying fixed over one point describes a geostationary orbit.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: The altitude of a geostationary satellite above the Earth's surface is approximately
cards.e: Only at about 35,786 km above the equator does one orbit take exactly one day. About 20,200 km is the altitude of GPS satellites.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Which of these sensors is a whiskbroom (across-track, oscillating-mirror) scanner?
cards.e: Landsat MSS and TM sweep the ground with an oscillating mirror. SPOT HRV, LISS and Cartosat cameras are pushbroom sensors with linear CCD arrays.

cards.q: For a pixel, near-infrared reflectance is 0.50 and red reflectance is 0.10. Its NDVI is about
cards.e: NDVI = (0.50 - 0.10) / (0.50 + 0.10) = 0.40 / 0.60 = 0.67. NDVI can never exceed 1, so 5.0 (the simple ratio) is not possible.

cards.q: Which surface cover normally gives a negative NDVI value?
cards.e: Water reflects less near-infrared than red, so the numerator becomes negative. All kinds of green vegetation give clearly positive values.

cards.q: Supervised image classification differs from unsupervised classification because it requires
o: training sites of known cover type
cards.e: In supervised classification the analyst first marks sample areas of each known class to train the classifier. Unsupervised methods cluster pixels first and need no training data.

cards.q: Which one of the following is an unsupervised classification method?
cards.e: ISODATA groups pixels into natural spectral clusters without training data. Maximum likelihood, minimum distance and parallelepiped all need training sites, so they are supervised.

cards.q: Which resampling method keeps the original pixel values unchanged during geometric correction?
cards.e: Nearest neighbour simply copies the value of the closest input pixel. Bilinear and cubic methods average 4 or 16 pixels and so create new values.

cards.q: Band ratio images are especially useful in mountainous terrain because they
o: reduce the effect of slope illumination and shadow
cards.e: Sunlit and shaded slopes of the same rock differ in brightness in every band, but the ratio between bands stays nearly the same. Ratios cannot improve pixel size or remove clouds.

cards.q: In remote sensing, the kappa coefficient is used to
o: express the accuracy of a classified map
cards.e: Kappa is calculated from the error (confusion) matrix and shows agreement beyond chance between the map and ground truth. It is not an enhancement or calibration tool.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: The chief advantage of microwave (radar) remote sensing over optical remote sensing is that it
o: works through cloud and at night
cards.e: Radar supplies its own energy and its long waves pass through cloud. Radar images actually have strong geometric distortions such as layover and shadow.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Which of the following radar bands has the longest wavelength?
cards.e: Wavelengths are roughly X 3 cm, C 5.6 cm, S 10 cm and L 23 cm. L-band therefore penetrates vegetation and dry soil the most.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: A calm lake appears very dark on a SAR image because
o: the smooth surface reflects the beam away from the antenna
the lake lies in radar shadow
cards.e: A smooth surface acts like a mirror (specular reflection), so the side-looking beam bounces away and little returns. Radar shadow occurs only behind tall features.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: On a radar image the top of a steep mountain is displaced towards the sensor and appears to lean over its base. This effect is called
cards.e: Layover occurs when the echo from the top returns before the echo from the base. Speckle is the grainy 'salt and pepper' noise of radar images.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: On a thermal infrared image acquired just before dawn, a lake normally appears
o: black because water emits no heat
the same as the surrounding land
cards.e: Water loses heat slowly, so at night it stays warmer than land. By day the pattern reverses and water appears cooler.

cards.q: In remote sensing geology, a 'lineament' is best described as
o: the line joining principal points of adjacent photos
any road or canal seen on an image
a mappable linear surface feature thought to reflect a subsurface structure
the flight line of the aircraft
cards.e: Lineaments are natural straight or gently curved features linked to faults, fractures or shear zones. Man-made lines such as roads must be removed during mapping.

cards.q: In a hard-rock (crystalline) terrain, the most favourable site for a high-yielding bore well is usually
cards.e: Lineament intersections mark zones of dense fracturing where water can be stored and can move. Inselbergs and massive outcrops shed rain as run-off.

cards.q: Which hydrogeomorphic unit generally has the best groundwater prospects?
cards.e: Valley fills hold thick loose sediment that stores and transmits water. The three hill units are run-off zones with thin or no weathered cover.

cards.q: Which statement about groundwater potential mapping with remote sensing and GIS is correct?
o: Steep slopes favour recharge more than gentle slopes
High drainage density usually indicates high infiltration
Bare rocky hills are given the highest weight
High lineament density usually improves groundwater potential in hard rock
cards.e: More lineaments mean more fractures to store and carry water. High drainage density and steep slope both point to quick run-off and poor recharge.

cards.q: Clay and other hydroxyl-bearing alteration minerals around ore bodies are detected by their absorption feature near
cards.e: The Al-OH bond absorbs near 2.2 µm, which is why Landsat TM band 7 and ASTER shortwave-infrared bands are used. Visible bands respond mainly to iron oxides, not clays.

cards.q: The first earth-resources satellite, Landsat-1 (ERTS-1), was launched in
cards.e: Landsat-1 was launched by the USA in July 1972. 1957 is Sputnik-1, 1986 is SPOT-1 and 1999 is Landsat 7.

cards.q: The Sentinel-1 satellites of the European Copernicus programme carry a
cards.e: Sentinel-1 is the radar mission, working in C-band. The 13-band multispectral imager is on Sentinel-2.

cards.q: India's first operational remote sensing satellite, IRS-1A, was launched in
cards.e: IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988. 1975 is Aryabhata, 1979 is the experimental Bhaskara-I and 1995 is IRS-1C.

cards.q: The sensors LISS-III, LISS-IV and AWiFS are carried together on which Indian satellite series?
cards.e: Resourcesat carries all three cameras for land-resource studies. Cartosat has high-resolution panchromatic cameras and RISAT carries radar.

cards.q: Which pair of satellite and main payload is correctly matched?
cards.e: Oceansat carries the Ocean Colour Monitor to map chlorophyll. C-band SAR belongs to RISAT-1, and LISS-IV to Resourcesat.

cards.q: India's first indigenously built radar imaging satellite, carrying a C-band SAR and launched in 2012, is
cards.e: RISAT-1 (April 2012) carried India's own C-band SAR. RISAT-2 was launched earlier, in 2009, but its X-band radar was built abroad.

cards.q: Chandrayaan-3 made its soft landing near the lunar south pole on
cards.e: The landing was on 23 August 2023, now marked as National Space Day. 6 January 2024 is the date Aditya-L1 reached its orbit around L1.

cards.q: Aditya-L1 observes the Sun from a halo orbit around the Lagrange point L1, which lies about
cards.e: L1 is about 1.5 million km from Earth on the line towards the Sun. 150 million km is the full Earth-Sun distance and 384,000 km is the Earth-Moon distance.

cards.q: NISAR, launched in July 2025, is a joint mission of ISRO and NASA that carries radars in which two bands?
cards.e: NASA supplied the L-band radar and ISRO the S-band radar, making NISAR the first dual-frequency SAR satellite. It was launched by GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota.

cards.q: Evidence of water molecules on the Moon's surface is credited to which Indian mission?
cards.e: Chandrayaan-1 (2008) carried NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper, which detected water and hydroxyl. Mangalyaan studied Mars and Aditya-L1 studies the Sun.

cards.q: The National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC), which distributes Indian satellite data, has its headquarters at
cards.e: NRSC is at Hyderabad, with its ground station at Shadnagar. Dehradun has IIRS (the training institute) and Ahmedabad has the Space Applications Centre.

cards.q: Bhuvan is
o: a radar imaging satellite launched in 2012
ISRO's web-based geoportal for maps and satellite imagery of India
cards.e: Bhuvan is the geoportal run by NRSC since 2009. India's navigation system is NavIC, which is the tempting wrong choice.

cards.q: The minimum number of GPS satellites that a receiver must track to fix its three-dimensional position is
cards.e: Three ranges give position and a fourth is needed to solve the receiver's clock error. Three satellites give only a rough 2D fix if the height is assumed.

cards.q: The near-global SRTM digital elevation model (2000) was produced by
o: radar interferometry from the Space Shuttle
cards.e: SRTM flew two radar antennas on Space Shuttle Endeavour and used the phase difference (interferometry) to get heights. Cartosat-1 stereo images produced the separate CartoDEM.

cards.q: Which satellite mission measures changes in the Earth's gravity field and has been used to estimate groundwater depletion in north-west India?
cards.e: GRACE senses tiny gravity changes caused by gain or loss of water mass. SRTM measured elevation, not gravity.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: Which of the following data sets is normally stored in raster format in a GIS?
cards.e: Elevation changes continuously, so it is stored as a grid of cells. Wells, roads and boundaries are discrete points, lines and polygons, which suit the vector model.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: In GIS, 'topology' refers to
o: spatial relationships such as adjacency and connectivity between features
the elevation of the land surface
the colour scheme of a map
cards.e: Topology records which features touch, connect or contain one another. Land elevation is topography, a similar-sounding but different word.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: A triangulated irregular network (TIN) is a
cards.e: A TIN joins irregularly spaced height points into triangles, so it is a vector surface model. The raster way of storing a surface is the grid DEM.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: To find all wells lying within 500 m of a river, the GIS operation to use first is
cards.e: A buffer creates a zone of fixed distance around the river; wells inside it are then selected by overlay. Georeferencing only ties a map to ground coordinates.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: In the UTM system, the State of Kerala falls in zone
cards.e: Zone 43 covers longitudes 72°E to 78°E, which includes all of Kerala (about 75°E to 77.5°E). Each UTM zone is 6° wide.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: In groundwater potential mapping, thematic layers such as geology, slope and lineament density are combined in a GIS by
cards.e: Each layer is given a weight and the layers are added cell by cell to get a potential index. Contrast stretching is only an image display enhancement.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Which change normally LOWERS the reflectance of a bare soil surface in visible and infrared bands?
o: Smoothing of a rough, ploughed surface
cards.e: Water in the soil absorbs light, so wet soil looks darker than dry soil. Less organic matter and a smoother surface both make soil brighter, not darker.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Which pairing of surface type and spectral behaviour is correct?
o: Fresh snow - very low reflectance in visible bands
Clear water - very low reflectance in near-infrared
Healthy vegetation - strong absorption in near-infrared
Dry bare soil - reflectance falls steadily from visible to shortwave infrared
cards.e: Clear water absorbs nearly all near-infrared energy. Vegetation reflects near-infrared strongly (it absorbs red and blue), dry soil reflectance rises with wavelength, and fresh snow is very bright in visible bands.

cards.q: After principal component analysis (PCA) of a six-band image, which output component carries the largest share of the total variance?
o: Each component carries an equal share
cards.e: PCA orders its components by variance, so PC1 always holds the most information and the last one is mostly noise. The shares are never equal when the bands are correlated.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: A scanner with an instantaneous field of view (IFOV) of 0.05 milliradian works from an altitude of 800 km. Its ground resolution cell at nadir is about
cards.e: Cell size = IFOV x height = 0.00005 x 800,000 m = 40 m. Forgetting to convert milliradian to radian or km to m gives answers wrong by factors of ten.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: Vertical aerial photos of 23 cm x 23 cm format are taken at a scale of 1:10,000 with 60% forward overlap. The air base (ground distance between successive exposures) is
cards.e: One photo covers 0.23 m x 10,000 = 2300 m. The aircraft moves forward only the non-overlapping 40%, so air base = 0.4 x 2300 = 920 m. The value 1380 m is the overlapped 60% part.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Using Wien's displacement law (constant 2898 µm K), the wavelength of peak emission from a fire at 800 K is about
cards.e: Peak wavelength = 2898 / 800 = 3.6 µm. This is why the 3-5 µm window is used to detect fires. About 9.7 µm is the peak for the normal Earth surface at 300 K.

cards.t: Concepts and principles of aerial photography and photogrammetry
cards.q: An aerial photograph that has been corrected for camera tilt and relief displacement, so that it has a uniform scale like a map, is called
cards.e: An orthophoto has the geometry of a map with the detail of a photo. An uncontrolled mosaic is only a set of photos pasted together, so it still carries tilt and relief errors.

cards.q: A 3 x 3 image window has the value 10 in eight pixels and 100 in the centre pixel. After a 3 x 3 mean (low-pass) filter, the centre pixel becomes
cards.e: Mean = (8 x 10 + 100) / 9 = 180 / 9 = 20. The value 10 would be the result of a median filter, which removes such a spike completely.

cards.t: Remote sensing in landform and land use mapping
cards.q: To map the conversion of paddy fields into built-up land in a Kerala district between 2005 and 2025, the main requirement is
o: one stereo pair of aerial photos of 2005
co-registered satellite images of both dates
a gravity survey of the district
cards.e: Change detection needs images of the same area from both dates that overlay exactly. A single-date image or stereo pair shows only the situation at one time.

cards.q: Which image feature is the strongest sign of a fault?
o: Smooth uniform grey tone over a plain
Abrupt offset of a ridge and stream along one straight line
A gradual change in vegetation up a hill slope
Even, fine dendritic drainage over a wide area
cards.e: A fault cuts and displaces beds, ridges and streams along a line. Dendritic drainage and uniform tone suggest uniform rock without strong structural control.

cards.q: Which statement about remote sensing in groundwater exploration is correct?
o: Thermal images show aquifers hundreds of metres below the surface
It maps surface indicators that must be confirmed by geophysical survey and drilling
Optical sensors measure the depth to the water table directly
It removes the need for test drilling
cards.e: Sensors see only the surface, so they show indicators such as landforms, lineaments and vegetation. Depth to water and aquifer thickness still need resistivity survey and drilling.

cards.q: Which type of remote sensing data is most useful for locating coastal springs and submarine groundwater discharge?
cards.e: Groundwater has a nearly constant temperature that differs from sea water, so its plume shows on thermal images. Panchromatic images show brightness only, and fresh and sea water look alike on them.

cards.q: For mapping iron-oxide (gossan) zones with Landsat Thematic Mapper data, the commonly used band ratio is
cards.e: Iron oxides reflect red (band 3) and absorb blue (band 1), so the 3/1 ratio is high over them. The 5/7 ratio is the tempting wrong choice; it picks out clay minerals, and 4/3 picks out vegetation.

cards.q: As of 2026, which two Landsat satellites are operating and together image the Earth every 8 days?
cards.e: Landsat 8 (2013) and Landsat 9 (2021) fly 8 days apart on the same 16-day cycle. Landsat 7 was decommissioned on 4 June 2025, and Landsat 6 never reached orbit.

cards.q: Which satellite navigation system is correctly paired with its owner?
cards.e: Galileo belongs to the European Union. GLONASS is Russian, BeiDou is Chinese and QZSS is Japan's regional system.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: Coordinates given by a GPS receiver are referred by default to which datum?
cards.e: GPS works on the global, earth-centred WGS 84 datum. Everest 1830 is the old ellipsoid of Survey of India maps, so GPS points may not fit old toposheets without conversion.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: A map projection that preserves angles, and so the shape of small areas, is called
cards.e: Conformal (orthomorphic) projections such as Mercator and UTM keep angles true. Equal-area projections keep area true but distort shape.

cards.t: Geographic Information System (GIS) - principles and applications
cards.q: A water-table contour map is to be prepared from water levels measured in 60 scattered observation wells. The GIS operation needed is
cards.e: Interpolation (for example IDW or kriging) estimates the water level between the wells to build a continuous surface. Buffering only draws distance zones around features.

cards.q: India's Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) entered orbit around Mars in
cards.e: It was launched on 5 November 2013 and entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014. So 2013 is the launch year, not the arrival year; 2008 is Chandrayaan-1.

cards.q: Cartosat-1 (2005) carried two panchromatic cameras, one tilted forward and one backward along the track, mainly to
o: obtain stereo pairs for mapping and elevation models
cards.e: Two views of the same ground from different angles give a stereo pair, from which heights are measured. India's CartoDEM was made this way. Ocean colour is the job of Oceansat.

cards.q: EOS-04, launched by PSLV-C52 in February 2022, is also known as
cards.e: EOS-04 is the C-band radar imaging satellite RISAT-1A. Oceansat-3 is the tempting wrong choice; it is EOS-06, launched in November 2022.

cards.q: India's first sounding rocket was launched on 21 November 1963 from
cards.e: Thumba, near the magnetic equator, was India's first rocket launching station and is now part of VSSC. Sriharikota became the satellite launch centre later.

cards.t: Remote sensing in landform and land use mapping
cards.q: The nodal agency of the Government of Kerala for remote sensing and GIS applications is
o: Kerala State Remote Sensing and Environment Centre (KSREC)
National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS)
Centre for Water Resources Development and Management (CWRDM)
cards.e: KSREC at Thiruvananthapuram is the State's remote sensing centre. NCESS is also at Thiruvananthapuram but is a Central Government earth science institute.

cards.t: Satellite remote sensing - data products and their interpretation
cards.q: Which one of the following is an ACTIVE remote sensing system?
cards.e: LiDAR sends out its own laser pulses and records their return. The other three only record sunlight reflected, or heat emitted, by the ground, so they are passive.

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: On a Flinn diagram, a strain ellipsoid with k = 0 has which shape?
o: Plane-strain ellipsoid with the Y axis unchanged
cards.e: k = 0 lies on the horizontal axis, where X = Y > Z: a flattened pancake. The cigar (prolate) shape is the opposite end, k = infinity. k = 1 is plane strain.

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: The Flinn diagram is a plot of:
o: the axial ratio X/Y against the axial ratio Y/Z
cards.e: Flinn plotted the two axial ratios of the strain ellipsoid, X/Y (vertical) against Y/Z (horizontal). Shear stress against normal stress is the Mohr diagram, which deals with stress, not strain shape.

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: Which strain-analysis method is correctly paired with the data it uses?
o: Wellman method — axial ratios of reduction spots
Rf/φ method — angles between hinge line and median line of deformed brachiopods
Fry method — distances between the centres of neighbouring grains or ooids
Flinn method — spacing of joints in a competent bed
cards.e: The Fry method is the centre-to-centre technique. Wellman's method is the one that uses deformed fossils such as brachiopods, and the Rf/φ method uses the shape and orientation of elliptical markers like pebbles.

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: A belemnite fossil originally 10 cm long has been stretched to 15 cm. Its quadratic elongation (λ) is:
cards.e: Elongation e = (15 − 10)/10 = 0.5. Stretch = 1 + e = 1.5. Quadratic elongation = (1 + e)² = 2.25. The values 0.5 and 1.5 are the elongation and the stretch, not λ.

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: Which statement about simple shear is correct?
o: It always involves a change in volume
It can occur only in brittle rocks
The principal strain axes keep the same orientation throughout the deformation
It is a rotational (non-coaxial) strain, like sliding a pack of cards
cards.e: In simple shear the strain axes rotate as deformation goes on, so it is non-coaxial. Axes that stay fixed describe pure shear (coaxial strain).

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: Which of these is NOT normally used as a strain marker?
cards.e: A strain marker needs a known shape before deformation: spots and ooids start as spheres, pebbles as rounded bodies. Columnar joints are cooling cracks, not objects that record later strain.

cards.t: Behaviour of minerals and rocks under deformation conditions
cards.q: Which change makes a rock more likely to break (brittle failure) instead of flowing?
cards.e: Rocks loaded quickly have no time to flow, so they snap. Heat, high confining pressure and slow loading all make rocks more ductile.

cards.q: In a rock, σ1 = 100 MPa and σ3 = 40 MPa. The maximum shear stress is:
cards.e: Maximum shear stress = (σ1 − σ3)/2 = 60/2 = 30 MPa, the radius of the Mohr circle. 70 MPa is the mean stress (the centre), and 60 MPa is the differential stress (the diameter).

cards.t: Behaviour of minerals and rocks under deformation conditions
cards.q: On a Mohr diagram, what happens when pore-fluid pressure rises while the total stresses stay the same?
o: The circle moves left, toward the failure envelope, with no change in size
The circle moves right, away from the failure envelope
The circle grows larger about the same centre
cards.e: Pore pressure is subtracted equally from every normal stress, so the whole circle shifts left by that amount. Its size stays the same because the differential stress has not changed.

cards.q: In Anderson's theory of faulting, thrust faults form when which principal stress is vertical?
cards.e: In thrusting the big squeeze (σ1) is horizontal and the smallest stress (σ3) is the vertical load. σ1 vertical gives normal faults; σ2 vertical gives strike-slip faults.

cards.q: According to Anderson's theory, a fault that forms with σ1 vertical should be a:
cards.e: Faults form at about 30° to σ1. With σ1 vertical the fault dips about 60° and the hanging wall slides down: a normal fault. A 30° thrust needs σ1 horizontal and σ3 vertical.

cards.q: Two conjugate shear fractures form together in a rock. Their line of intersection is parallel to:
o: the bisector of σ1 and σ3
cards.e: Both fracture planes contain the σ2 direction, so they meet along it. σ1 is not the intersection; it bisects the acute angle between the two fractures.

cards.t: Behaviour of minerals and rocks under deformation conditions
cards.q: A fine-grained, strongly foliated rock formed by ductile shearing with grain-size reduction is:
cards.e: Mylonite forms where rock flows in a ductile shear zone and its grains recrystallise smaller. Breccia and gouge are broken (brittle) fault rocks, and pseudotachylite is glass from frictional melting.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A bed is offset by a normal fault with a throw of 173 m and a heave of 100 m. The dip of the fault plane is about:
cards.e: tan(dip) = throw / heave = 173/100 = 1.73, so dip = 60°. The value 30° is the hade (angle from the vertical), which comes from heave / throw.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A fault has a strike-slip component of 30 m and a dip-slip component of 40 m. Its net slip is:
cards.e: The two components are at right angles on the fault plane, so net slip = √(30² + 40²) = 50 m. Simply adding them (70 m) is wrong because they are not in the same direction.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: An isolated remnant of a thrust sheet, cut off from the main sheet by erosion and resting on the rocks below the thrust, is a:
cards.e: A klippe is an erosional outlier of a nappe or thrust sheet. A window is the opposite: a hole eroded through the sheet that shows the rocks underneath.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
p: TNPSC Geology paper (code 394, year not stated)
cards.q: Which statement about a tectonic window (fenster) is correct?
o: It is a gap in the rock record caused by non-deposition
It is a block dropped down between two normal faults
It is a remnant of a thrust sheet completely isolated by erosion
Erosion has cut through a thrust sheet and exposed the rocks lying below the thrust
cards.e: A window is an erosional hole in a thrust sheet, ringed by the thrust, showing the lower rocks. The isolated remnant of the sheet is a klippe, and the dropped block is a graben.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A horst is:
o: a fold with a horizontal axial plane
a rock sheet thrust over younger rocks
a down-dropped block bounded by normal faults
an uplifted block bounded by normal faults
cards.e: A horst stands high between two normal faults that dip away from it. The down-dropped block between normal faults is a graben.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Which of these is NOT a field criterion for recognising a fault?
o: Triangular facets along a straight scarp
A basal conglomerate lying on an old erosion surface
cards.e: A basal conglomerate marks an unconformity: it is the first deposit on an eroded surface. Slickensides, breccia, gouge and triangular facets are all made by fault movement.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: By Fleuty's classification, a fold with an interlimb angle of 50° is:
cards.e: Close folds have interlimb angles of 70° to 30°. Open folds are 120° to 70°, gentle folds are above 120°, and isoclinal folds have parallel limbs (0°).

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: In Ramsay's classification, similar folds (dip isogons parallel to each other) belong to:
cards.e: Class 2 folds have parallel isogons and identical shapes in every layer. Class 1B is the parallel (concentric) fold, with convergent isogons at right angles to the layer.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A parallel (concentric) fold keeps the same thickness when measured at right angles to the layer. In Ramsay's scheme it is:
cards.e: Constant orthogonal thickness defines Class 1B. Class 2 (similar folds) keeps constant thickness measured parallel to the axial plane instead, so its hinges look thick.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A fold whose hinge line plunges directly down the dip of its inclined axial plane is called a:
cards.e: In a reclined fold the hinge pitches at about 90° on the inclined axial plane. A recumbent fold is different: its axial plane and hinge are both nearly horizontal.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
p: TNPSC Geology paper (code 394, year not stated)
cards.q: A fold with two hinges and three limbs, giving a roughly rectangular profile, is a:
cards.e: A box fold is a conjugate fold with a flat top and two hinge zones. A chevron fold has only one sharp hinge and two straight limbs.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A fold is arch-shaped (closes upward), but its core holds the youngest rocks. It is best called:
cards.e: Antiform describes the arch shape; syncline means youngest rocks in the core. A synformal anticline is the reverse: trough-shaped with the oldest rocks in the core.

cards.q: Which feature is typical of flexural-slip folding?
o: Slip on closely spaced planes parallel to the axial plane
Layers much thicker at the hinge than on the limbs
Slickensides on bedding planes at right angles to the fold hinge
Folds found only in massive, unlayered rock
cards.e: Beds slide over one another like bent cards, scratching the bedding planes across the hinge. Slip on planes parallel to the axial plane is passive (shear) folding, which gives thick hinges.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Slaty cleavage that is parallel to the axial planes of folds forms:
o: parallel to the direction of greatest shortening
at right angles to the direction of greatest shortening (parallel to the XY plane of the strain ellipsoid)
parallel to bedding everywhere in the fold
cards.e: Platy minerals line up flat-on to the squeeze, so cleavage is perpendicular to Z, the shortest strain axis. It cannot be parallel to the shortening direction.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: In one outcrop, bedding dips 70° east and axial-plane cleavage dips 40° east. The beds here are most likely:
o: on the overturned limb of a fold
on the normal (right-way-up) limb of a fold
cards.e: When bedding is steeper than cleavage and both dip the same way, the beds are overturned. On a normal limb the cleavage would be the steeper of the two.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Crenulation cleavage is produced by:
o: shrinking of lava as it cools
flow of magma against a chamber wall
cards.e: Small wrinkles (crenulations) in an older foliation line up to make a new cleavage, so it proves a second deformation. Cooling and unloading produce joints, not cleavage.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Which of these is NOT a lineation?
cards.e: Schistosity is a planar fabric (a foliation) made by parallel mica flakes. Mullions, rods and slickenlines are all linear structures.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Which joint type is correctly matched with its description?
o: Columnar joints — formed by tectonic compression of sandstone
Sheet joints — formed by unloading of massive rock such as granite
Mural joints — a single set of joints found in shale
Longitudinal joints — joints at right angles to the fold axis
cards.e: Sheet (exfoliation) joints open parallel to the surface when overlying rock is removed. Columnar joints are cooling cracks, mural joints are three sets in granite, and longitudinal joints run parallel to the fold axis.

cards.q: Ramsay's Type 1 interference pattern, formed when two sets of upright folds cross at a high angle, looks like:
cards.e: Crossing arches make domes and crossing troughs make basins. Mushroom and crescent shapes are Type 2, and hooks are Type 3.

cards.q: Refolding in which the two fold axes are nearly parallel but the axial planes are at a high angle (coaxial refolding) gives Ramsay's:
cards.e: Sharing one axis direction, the early fold is simply bent again, giving a hook shape. Type 1 needs fold axes that cross at a high angle.

cards.q: A garnet with spiral (S-shaped) inclusion trails that pass smoothly into the matrix foliation grew:
cards.e: The crystal rotated while it was growing, so it trapped a spiral (snowball garnet): syn-tectonic growth. A post-tectonic crystal would have straight trails and would not have rotated.

cards.q: Which observation best shows that a porphyroblast is post-tectonic?
o: It cuts across the foliation, and its straight inclusion trails run on into the matrix foliation
The foliation wraps around it and pressure shadows are present
It is cracked, bent and shows wavy extinction
cards.e: A crystal that grew after deformation overprints the finished fabric without disturbing it. Wrapping foliation and pressure shadows mean the crystal was there before the deformation (pre-tectonic).

cards.q: Sandstone beds resting on an eroded surface of granite form a:
cards.e: Sediments lying on eroded plutonic or massive metamorphic rock make a nonconformity. An angular unconformity needs tilted layered rocks below, which granite does not have.

cards.q: Beds above and below a contact are parallel and no erosion surface can be seen, but fossils show a large time gap. This is a:
cards.e: A paraconformity looks like an ordinary bedding plane; only fossils reveal the gap. A disconformity also has parallel beds but shows a visible, uneven erosion surface.

cards.q: The Eparchaean Unconformity exposed at Tirumala (Andhra Pradesh) separates:
o: Gondwana rocks from the Deccan Traps
Archaean basement from Proterozoic Cuddapah rocks
cards.e: At Tirumala, Cuddapah quartzite lies on eroded Archaean granite and gneiss. The name means 'after the Archaean', so it cannot involve the much younger Gondwana or Deccan rocks.

cards.q: Erosion of the crest of an anticline exposes older rocks completely surrounded by younger rocks of the normal sequence. This outcrop is:
cards.e: Older rocks ringed by younger rocks make an inlier. An outlier is the reverse: a patch of younger rock surrounded by older rock.

cards.q: Which statement describes thin-skinned tectonics?
o: Basement blocks are faulted up through the cover along steep faults
Cover rocks fold and thrust above a detachment (décollement) while the basement stays largely uninvolved
Deformation is limited to the mantle
cards.e: The cover slides and crumples on a weak layer such as salt or shale, like a rug on a floor. When the basement is faulted too, it is thick-skinned tectonics.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A bed has a true dip of 45°. In a vertical section that makes an angle of 30° with the strike, the apparent dip is about:
cards.e: tan(apparent dip) = tan 45° × sin 30° = 1 × 0.5 = 0.5, so the apparent dip is about 27°. Using cos 30° by mistake gives 41°. Apparent dip is always less than true dip.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: On flat ground, a bed dipping at 30° has an outcrop width of 100 m measured at right angles to strike. Its true thickness is:
cards.e: True thickness = outcrop width × sin(dip) = 100 × 0.5 = 50 m. The value 58 m (100 × tan 30°) is the vertical thickness, which is always more than the true thickness.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: On a geological map, the outcrop of a vertical dyke crossing a valley:
o: runs straight across, unaffected by the contours
cards.e: A vertical sheet is not shifted sideways by changes in ground height, so its outcrop is a straight line. Outcrops that follow the contours belong to horizontal beds.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Where it crosses a valley, a bed's outcrop makes a V that points downstream. The bed:
o: dips downstream at an angle steeper than the valley floor
cards.e: By the rule of V's, the V points in the direction of dip, so the bed dips downstream. Horizontal beds and beds dipping upstream both V upstream.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: To contour the density of poles to planes in structural geology, the net normally used is the:
cards.e: Only an equal-area net keeps the density of points undistorted, which contouring needs. The Wulff net keeps angles true and is the one used in crystallography.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: On a lower-hemisphere stereonet, a vertical plane plots as:
o: a straight line through the centre
a small circle near the edge
a single point at the centre
cards.e: A vertical plane passes through the centre of the sphere top to bottom, so its trace is a diameter. The outer circle is a horizontal plane, and the centre point is a vertical line.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: In a π-diagram of a cylindrical fold, poles to bedding fall along a great circle. The pole of that great circle gives the:
cards.e: Every bedding plane in a cylindrical fold contains the fold axis, so all their poles lie 90° from it, on one great circle. The axial plane needs extra data, such as the axial trace.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: On a flat erosion surface, the outcrop of a plunging anticline shows:
o: concentric rings with the youngest beds in the centre
a nose that closes in the direction of plunge, with the oldest beds in the core
a nose that closes opposite to the plunge, with the youngest beds in the core
cards.e: An anticline keeps its oldest beds in the core, and its outcrop closes toward the plunge. A plunging syncline does the opposite: youngest beds in the core, closing away from the plunge.

cards.t: Structural behaviour of igneous rocks, diapirs and salt domes
cards.q: From bottom to top, the usual cap-rock sequence above a salt dome is:
cards.e: Anhydrite is left behind when groundwater dissolves the top of the salt, so it sits next to the salt. Higher up it changes to gypsum and then calcite, where native sulphur is found.

cards.t: Structural behaviour of igneous rocks, diapirs and salt domes
cards.q: Salt rises through overlying sediments as diapirs mainly because:
o: salt is denser than every sedimentary rock
salt swells when it absorbs groundwater
buried salt is lighter than the compacted sediments above it and can flow
cards.e: Sediments get denser with burial but salt stays near 2.2 g/cm³, so deep salt is buoyant and creeps upward. Salt does not melt; it flows as a soft solid.

cards.t: Structural behaviour of igneous rocks, diapirs and salt domes
cards.q: Which intrusion is correctly matched with its form?
o: Laccolith — saucer-shaped body sagging in the middle
Phacolith — lens-shaped body along the crest or trough of a fold
Sill — sheet cutting steeply across the bedding
Lopolith — dome-shaped body with a flat floor
cards.e: A phacolith fills the space at a fold hinge. The other three are swapped: the laccolith is the dome with a flat floor, the lopolith is the saucer, and the sheet that cuts across bedding is a dyke.

cards.t: Structural behaviour of igneous rocks, diapirs and salt domes
cards.q: Cone sheets differ from ring dykes because cone sheets:
o: are always parallel to the bedding
dip inward toward a common centre at depth
are vertical or dip steeply outward
form only in bodies of rock salt
cards.e: Cone sheets fill inward-dipping cracks opened by upward magma pressure. Ring dykes are vertical or dip outward and form when a central block sinks (cauldron subsidence).

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Structure contours on a coal seam have a vertical interval of 58 m and are spaced 100 m apart on the map. The dip of the seam is about:
cards.e: tan(dip) = vertical interval / horizontal spacing = 58/100 = 0.58, so dip is about 30°. A 45° dip would need the spacing to equal the interval.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: The Main Boundary Thrust (MBT) of the Himalaya separates:
o: the Siwaliks from the Indo-Gangetic plain
the Tethys Himalaya from the Higher Himalaya
the Higher Himalaya from the Lesser Himalaya
the Lesser Himalaya from the Siwalik (Sub-Himalaya) belt
cards.e: Along the MBT, Lesser Himalayan rocks ride over the Siwaliks. The Higher–Lesser Himalaya boundary is the Main Central Thrust, and the Siwalik–plains boundary is the Main Frontal Thrust.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: The Achankovil Shear Zone of southern Kerala lies between:
o: the Western Dharwar and Eastern Dharwar cratons
the Madurai Block and the Trivandrum Block
the Cuddapah Basin and the Eastern Ghats belt
the Dharwar Craton and the Deccan Traps
cards.e: This NW–SE shear zone divides the Madurai Block to the north from the Trivandrum Block (Kerala Khondalite Belt) to the south. The other pairs lie far outside Kerala.

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: Which statement correctly separates stress from strain?
o: Stress is the permanent part of deformation; strain is the recoverable part
Stress is measured in metres; strain is measured in pascals
Stress is force per unit area; strain is the resulting change in shape or volume and has no units
Stress is change in length per unit length; strain is force per unit area
cards.e: Stress is the cause (force on an area, in pascals). Strain is the effect, a ratio with no units. The first distractor simply swaps the two definitions.

cards.t: Measurement of strain in deformed rocks
cards.q: In a strain ellipsoid with axes X ≥ Y ≥ Z, the direction of maximum shortening is parallel to:
o: the bisector of the X and Y axes
cards.e: Z is the shortest axis, so it is the squeeze direction. X is the direction of greatest stretching; cleavage forms in the XY plane, at right angles to Z.

cards.q: On a Mohr stress circle, the centre of the circle on the normal-stress axis gives the:
cards.e: The circle runs from σ3 to σ1 on the horizontal axis, so its centre is their average. The maximum shear stress is the radius, and the differential stress is the diameter.

cards.q: In a rock, σ1 = 90 MPa and σ3 = 30 MPa. The normal stress on a plane whose normal makes 60° with σ1 is:
cards.e: σn = (σ1 + σ3)/2 + [(σ1 − σ3)/2] cos 2θ = 60 + 30 × cos 120° = 60 − 15 = 45 MPa. Using θ = 30° by mistake gives 75 MPa; 60 MPa is only the mean stress.

cards.t: Behaviour of minerals and rocks under deformation conditions
cards.q: A material in which stress is proportional to the strain rate, not to the strain, behaves as:
cards.e: Viscous flow depends on how fast the material is strained; the dashpot is its model. In an elastic solid stress is proportional to strain itself (Hooke's law).

cards.t: Behaviour of minerals and rocks under deformation conditions
cards.q: Stylolites in limestone are produced mainly by:
cards.e: Calcite dissolves along a stressed surface and the insoluble clay is left as a dark, toothed seam. Twinning does deform calcite, but it happens inside crystals and does not remove rock.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: The angle between a slickenline and the strike line of the fault plane, measured within the fault plane itself, is the:
cards.e: Pitch or rake is measured in the plane that holds the line. Plunge is the angle between the line and the horizontal, measured in a vertical plane.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A lineation lies on a plane that dips 30°, and its pitch on that plane is 90°. The plunge of the lineation is:
cards.e: A pitch of 90° means the line runs straight down the dip, so its plunge equals the dip of the plane, 30°. (In general, sin plunge = sin pitch × sin dip.) A pitch of 0° would give a plunge of 0°.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: A bed strikes N–S and dips 30° east. Its apparent dip in a vertical section trending N45°E is about:
cards.e: The section makes 45° with the strike. tan(apparent dip) = tan 30° × sin 45° = 0.577 × 0.707 = 0.41, so about 22°. It must be less than the true dip of 30°.

cards.q: Folds produced by compression acting parallel to the layering of a competent bed are formed by:
cards.e: Buckling needs end-on (layer-parallel) compression, like pushing the ends of a ruler together. Bending is caused by forces acting across the layer, for example over a rising intrusion.

cards.q: Small parasitic folds are S- or Z-shaped on the limbs of a large fold. In the hinge zone of the large fold they are typically:
o: absent, because the hinge is never folded
cards.e: At the hinge the two limbs of each small fold are equal, so the shape is a symmetrical M or W. The asymmetric S and Z shapes belong to the two opposite limbs.

cards.q: A normal fault that is concave upward, flattens with depth and has a rollover anticline in its hanging wall is a:
cards.e: Listric means shovel-shaped. The hanging wall bends down against the curved fault to form the rollover. Transform and wrench faults are strike-slip faults, and imbricate thrusts are compressional.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Looking across a strike-slip fault, an observer sees that a stream on the far side has been shifted to the left. The fault is:
cards.e: Far side moved left = left-lateral, or sinistral. It would be dextral if the far side had moved to the right. The result is the same whichever side you stand on.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Along a traverse across the strike, beds crop out in the order P-Q-R-P-Q-R, all dipping the same way at the same angle. The repetition is best explained by:
cards.e: A fault repeats beds in the same order. A fold would repeat them in mirror-image order (P-Q-R-Q-P) and the dips would change across the axis.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Extension (tension) joints form:
o: as conjugate pairs at about 30° to σ1
at right angles to σ1, the greatest compressive stress
parallel to σ3 and at right angles to σ2
at right angles to σ3, the least compressive stress
cards.e: A crack opens in the direction of least squeeze, so its plane is perpendicular to σ3 and contains σ1. Conjugate pairs at about 30° to σ1 are shear fractures, not extension joints.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Which feature would NOT help to find the way-up (top and bottom) of steeply dipping beds?
cards.e: Slickensides are made by fault slip and say nothing about the original top of a bed. Graded bedding, cross-bedding and mud cracks are primary structures with a clear top and bottom.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: The Narmada–Son Lineament of central India trends approximately:
cards.e: It follows the Satpura trend, ENE–WSW, and the Narmada flows west along it. NW–SE is the trend of the Godavari and Mahanadi rifts; NNW–SSE is the Dharwar trend.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: Which Himalayan structure is correctly matched with the units it separates?
o: Indus–Tsangpo Suture — Siwaliks over the Ganga plain
Main Boundary Thrust — Tethys Himalaya over the Higher Himalaya
Main Central Thrust — Higher Himalayan crystallines over the Lesser Himalaya
Main Frontal Thrust — Lesser Himalaya over the Higher Himalaya
cards.e: The MCT carries the Higher Himalayan crystalline rocks south over the Lesser Himalaya. The MBT puts the Lesser Himalaya over the Siwaliks, and the MFT puts the Siwaliks over the plains.

cards.t: Structural analysis of folds, cleavages, lineations, joints and faults
cards.q: The Palghat Gap, the widest break in the Western Ghats, lies along the:
cards.e: The gap follows the east–west Palghat–Cauvery Shear Zone. The Achankovil Shear Zone is also in Kerala but lies farther south and trends NW–SE.

cards.q: Which observation is the clearest sign that an area was folded twice?
o: Beds are thicker at fold hinges than on the limbs
Bedding planes carry slickensides at right angles to the hinges
All folds plunge gently in the same direction
The axial-plane cleavage of the early folds is itself folded
cards.e: An axial-plane cleavage forms as a set of planes, so if it is now folded a later folding must have bent it. Thick hinges and bedding slickensides only tell you how a single fold formed.

cards.q: Early recumbent folds are refolded by upright folds whose axes are at a high angle to the early axes. On a flat erosion surface the outcrop shapes are:
cards.e: Both the axial planes and the hinges of the early folds get bent, giving mushroom and crescent shapes. Domes and basins need two sets of upright folds; hooks need parallel fold axes.

cards.q: Large eye-shaped feldspar grains that survived grain-size reduction in a mylonite are called:
cards.e: A porphyroclast is an old grain left over while the matrix was ground down and recrystallized. A porphyroblast is the opposite: a new crystal that grew during metamorphism.

cards.q: Straight inclusion trails inside a staurolite crystal lie at a high angle to the matrix foliation and stop sharply at the crystal edge. The crystal most likely grew:
o: from a melt, before any metamorphism
after an early foliation formed but before the present matrix foliation (inter-tectonic)
while rotating during the latest deformation (syn-tectonic)
cards.e: The trails record an older foliation that the crystal overgrew; later deformation made a new foliation outside. A post-tectonic crystal would have trails that run on into the matrix foliation.

cards.q: A metamorphic rock made of strain-free polygonal quartz grains meeting at 120° triple junctions shows that:
o: the quartz was melted by friction on a fault
the grains were crushed by brittle faulting
deformation continued long after crystallization stopped
cards.e: Heat lets strained grains regrow into strain-free polygons once the squeezing stops. If deformation had gone on longer, the grains would show wavy extinction and bent or elongated shapes.

cards.q: During a marine transgression each younger bed extends farther onto the old land surface than the bed below it. This relation is called:
cards.e: As the sea advances, each new bed reaches farther landward and overlaps the one below. Offlap is the reverse pattern, formed while the sea retreats.

cards.q: Which is the best field evidence that a contact is an unconformity and not a fault or an intrusive contact?
o: A chilled margin and baked country rock
A basal conglomerate containing pebbles of the underlying rock
cards.e: Pebbles of the lower rock in the first bed above prove the lower rock was exposed and eroded. Gouge and mylonite point to a fault, and a chilled margin points to an intrusion.

cards.q: In Rajasthan, the basement on which the Aravalli Supergroup was deposited is the:
cards.e: The Archaean Banded Gneissic Complex lies below the Aravalli rocks with an erosional unconformity. The Vindhyan, Malani and Deccan rocks are all younger than the Aravalli Supergroup.

cards.t: Structural behaviour of igneous rocks, diapirs and salt domes
cards.q: In Cloos's scheme of primary joints in a granite pluton, cross (Q) joints are:
o: at right angles to the flow lines
steep and parallel to the flow lines
cards.e: Q joints open by stretching along the flow direction, so they cut across the flow lines. Steep joints parallel to the flow lines are the longitudinal (S) joints, and flat ones are L joints.

cards.t: Structural behaviour of igneous rocks, diapirs and salt domes
cards.q: Which is NOT a typical feature of a salt dome?
o: A cap rock of anhydrite, gypsum and calcite
A rim syncline around the dome
Radial normal faults in the arched beds above it
A gravity high, because salt is denser than the surrounding sediments
cards.e: Salt is lighter than compacted sediments, so a salt dome gives a gravity low, not a high. Cap rock, rim syncline and radial faults are all normal features of salt domes.

cards.t: Structural behaviour of igneous rocks, diapirs and salt domes
cards.q: Rock salt makes a good seal for oil and gas traps on the flanks of a salt dome because salt is:
o: practically impermeable and flows to heal any fractures
cards.e: Salt has almost no connected pore space and creeps shut around cracks, so fluids cannot pass. A porous and permeable rock would be a reservoir, not a seal.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
cards.q: Which statement expresses Walther's Law of facies?
o: An intrusion is younger than the rock it cuts
Fossil assemblages succeed each other in a fixed order
Facies that lie one above another in a conformable sequence were once deposited side by side
In an undisturbed sequence the lowest bed is the oldest
cards.e: Walther linked vertical stacking of facies to their sideways arrangement. The 'lowest bed is oldest' rule is Steno's superposition, not Walther's law.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
cards.q: The fundamental mappable unit of lithostratigraphy is the
cards.e: Geological maps are built from formations. A member is only a part of a formation, and a group is a set of formations.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
cards.q: The chronostratigraphic (time-rock) unit that corresponds to a geological Period is the
cards.e: Rocks formed during a Period make a System, e.g. the Jurassic System. Series matches Epoch, which is the next lower rank.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
p: Kerala University M.Sc. Geology model questions (GL 231)
cards.q: The principle that fossil assemblages succeed one another in a definite and recognisable order is credited to
cards.e: William Smith saw this while surveying canals and used it to map England. Steno gave the physical laws (superposition etc.), which do not involve fossils.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
p: Calicut Univ M.Sc. Applied Geology 'Stratigraphy and Indian Geology' Nov 2024
cards.q: Which of the following is NOT one of Steno's laws?
cards.e: Steno (1669) gave superposition, original horizontality and lateral continuity. Faunal succession came much later from William Smith.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
p: Kerala University M.Sc. Geology model questions (GL 231)
cards.q: A GSSP ('golden spike') defines
o: the base of a chronostratigraphic unit at a fixed point in a chosen rock section
the top of a formation at its type locality
a boundary by a round-number age without any reference section
the thickest known section of a system
cards.e: A GSSP fixes the lower boundary of a stage at one point in one section. A boundary set only by a round-number age is a GSSA, used for most of the Precambrian.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
cards.q: A biozone defined by the natural association of three or more fossil taxa, without regard to their individual ranges, is
cards.e: An assemblage zone uses a group of taxa found together. An acme zone is based on the peak abundance of a single taxon.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
cards.q: Which sequence lists lithostratigraphic units correctly from highest to lowest rank?
cards.e: Supergroup is the largest and Bed the smallest. A common slip is to put Formation above Group; a group is made of formations.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
cards.q: Pick the odd one out: which of these is a geochronologic (time) unit, while the other three are chronostratigraphic (rock) units?
cards.e: Epoch is a span of time. System, Series and Stage are bodies of rock formed during a Period, Epoch and Age.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Nomenclature and the modern stratigraphic code
cards.q: A beach sandstone formation was laid down by a slowly advancing sea, so its base is older in the west than in the east. Such a unit is described as
cards.e: Diachronous means the rock boundary cuts across time lines. Isochronous means the same age everywhere, which is true only of chronostratigraphic boundaries.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The stable daughter product of uranium-235 is
cards.e: U-235 ends at Pb-207. Pb-206 is the tempting wrong choice, but it comes from U-238; Pb-208 comes from Th-232 and Pb-204 is not radiogenic.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Potassium-40 changes to argon-40 by
cards.e: About 11% of K-40 captures an electron and becomes Ar-40. Beta emission is the other branch, but that produces calcium-40, not argon.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: A mineral retains only 12.5% of its original potassium-40 (half-life 1.25 billion years). Assuming a closed system, its age is about
cards.e: 12.5% is 1/8, which means three half-lives. 3 x 1.25 = 3.75 billion years; two half-lives would leave 25%.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: In an Rb-Sr whole-rock isochron diagram, the intercept of the isochron on the vertical axis gives the
cards.e: The intercept is the strontium ratio the rock started with, and it tells us about the source. The age comes from the slope, not the intercept.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The half-life of carbon-14 is about
cards.e: C-14 halves every 5,730 years, so it works only up to about 50,000 years. 57,300 years is roughly its useful limit, not its half-life.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
cards.q: An Archean komatiite (ultramafic lava) is poor in potassium, rubidium and zircon and has been metamorphosed. Which system is most suitable to date it?
cards.e: Sm and Nd are present in mafic-ultramafic rocks and are not disturbed easily by metamorphism. K-Ar and Rb-Sr need K-rich minerals and are reset by heating.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The mineral most widely used for U-Pb dating, because it accepts uranium but excludes lead when it crystallises, is
cards.e: Zircon starts with almost no lead, so its lead is from decay, and it is very tough. Biotite and glauconite are used for K-Ar and Rb-Sr dating instead.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Fission tracks used for dating apatite and zircon are produced mainly by
cards.e: A U-238 nucleus sometimes splits in two, and the fragments leave a damage trail. Alpha decay is far more common but does not make etchable tracks.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Which of these parent isotopes has the longest half-life?
