cards.e: Sm-147 has a half-life of about 106 billion years. Rb-87 is next at about 49 billion years; U-238 (4.47) and K-40 (1.25) are far shorter.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: In the 40Ar/39Ar dating method, the sample is first irradiated with neutrons in order to
cards.e: Argon-39 made from potassium-39 stands in for the potassium content, so only argon isotopes need be measured. Atmospheric argon is corrected for using argon-36, not removed by irradiation.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Which mineral-method pair has the LOWEST closure temperature?
cards.e: Apatite fission tracks are kept only below about 110 degrees C. Biotite K-Ar closes near 300 degrees C, hornblende near 500 degrees C and zircon U-Pb above 900 degrees C.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Which isotope is most suitable to show that groundwater was recharged within the last few decades?
cards.e: Tritium has a half-life of only about 12.3 years and entered rain in large amounts after 1950s bomb tests. Carbon-14 suits old groundwater, thousands of years in age.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: A K-Ar age that is younger than the true age of a rock is most commonly caused by
o: excess potassium added by weathering only
loss of radiogenic argon during later heating
a decay constant that changes with temperature
cards.e: Argon is a gas and leaks out when the rock is reheated, so the clock is partly reset. Excess argon has the opposite effect and gives ages that are too old.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Kerala University M.Sc. Geology model questions (GL 231)
cards.q: Which is the correct order of eons from oldest to youngest?
cards.e: Hadean is first, then Archean, Proterozoic and Phanerozoic. The usual slip is to swap Archean and Proterozoic; Archean ('ancient') is the older one.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: According to the current International Chronostratigraphic Chart (v2026/06), the base of the Cambrian System is at
cards.e: The Cambrian, and the Phanerozoic, start at 538.8 Ma. 251.9 Ma is the Permian-Triassic boundary and 66.0 Ma is the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
cards.q: The largest mass extinction in Earth history took place at the end of the
cards.e: The end-Permian event (about 252 Ma) removed about 90% of marine species. The end-Cretaceous event is more famous because of the dinosaurs, but it was smaller.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: On the current ICS chart the base of the Quaternary System is placed at
cards.e: The Quaternary starts at 2.58 Ma (base of the Gelasian Stage), fixed in 2009. 0.0117 Ma is the base of the Holocene, and 5.33 Ma is the base of the Pliocene.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The GSSP for the Meghalayan Stage, the youngest stage of the Holocene, is located in
o: a stalagmite from Mawmluh Cave, Meghalaya
a marine section at El Kef, Tunisia
a lake core from Crawford Lake, Canada
cards.e: The Meghalayan base (about 4,200 years ago) is fixed in a Mawmluh Cave stalagmite. The Greenland ice core defines the base of the Holocene itself, 11,700 years ago.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Which of the following periods does NOT belong to the Palaeozoic Era?
cards.e: The Triassic is the first period of the Mesozoic. The Permian is the last Palaeozoic period and is the usual confusion.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The Ordovician System was proposed in 1879, to settle the dispute over overlapping Cambrian and Silurian strata in Wales, by
cards.e: Lapworth placed the disputed beds in a new system. Sedgwick (Cambrian) and Murchison (Silurian) were the two sides of the quarrel.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
cards.q: The Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary (66 Ma) is recognised worldwide by a thin clay layer enriched in
cards.e: Iridium is rare in the crust but common in meteorites, so the layer points to an impact. Uranium enrichment marks some black shales but is not the boundary marker.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The Archean-Proterozoic boundary is fixed at
cards.e: It is a round-number age (GSSA) of 2500 Ma. 4031 Ma is the base of the Archean and 1600 Ma is the base of the Mesoproterozoic.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Which is the correct order of Cenozoic epochs from oldest to youngest?
o: Eocene - Paleocene - Oligocene - Pliocene - Miocene - Pleistocene - Holocene
Paleocene - Eocene - Oligocene - Miocene - Pliocene - Pleistocene - Holocene
Paleocene - Eocene - Miocene - Oligocene - Pliocene - Pleistocene - Holocene
Paleocene - Oligocene - Eocene - Miocene - Pliocene - Pleistocene - Holocene
cards.e: Hook: 'Put Eggs On My Plate Please, Honey'. The usual slip is to swap Eocene and Oligocene, or Oligocene and Miocene.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The Cryogenian and Ediacaran periods belong to the
cards.e: The Neoproterozoic (1000-538.8 Ma) has the Tonian, Cryogenian and Ediacaran. The Ediacaran is just before the Cambrian but is still Precambrian, not Palaeozoic.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Stratigraphic procedures of correlation of unfossiliferous rocks
p: Kerala University M.Sc. Geology model questions (GL 231)
cards.q: The present-day normal polarity chron, which began about 0.78 million years ago, is the
cards.e: We live in the Brunhes normal chron. The Matuyama came just before it but was reversed.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Stratigraphic procedures of correlation of unfossiliferous rocks
cards.q: Which of the following makes the best marker (key) bed for correlating unfossiliferous sequences over a wide area?
o: A local coal seam in one sub-basin
cards.e: An ash fall is thin, distinctive, widespread and laid down in days, so it is a time line. Channel sandstones and conglomerate lenses are local and form at different times in different places.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Stratigraphic procedures of correlation of unfossiliferous rocks
p: Calicut Univ M.Sc. Applied Geology 'Stratigraphy and Indian Geology' Nov 2024
cards.q: In sequence stratigraphy, a depositional sequence is bounded by
o: first and last appearances of an index fossil
cards.e: Sequence boundaries are erosion surfaces formed when sea level falls, traced seaward into conformable surfaces. Units bounded by marine flooding surfaces are parasequences, which are smaller.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Stratigraphic procedures of correlation of unfossiliferous rocks
cards.q: In the marine oxygen-isotope stage (MIS) scheme, odd-numbered stages represent
cards.e: Odd stages are warm, starting with stage 1, the Holocene. Even stages such as stage 2 (last glacial maximum) are cold.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Stratigraphic procedures of correlation of unfossiliferous rocks
cards.q: Pick the odd one out: which correlation tool CANNOT be used in rocks that have no fossils?
cards.e: A concurrent-range zone is defined by overlapping ranges of fossil taxa, so it needs fossils. The other three are physical methods that work in barren rocks.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.t: Stratigraphic procedures of correlation of unfossiliferous rocks
cards.q: The maximum flooding surface in a depositional sequence separates the
o: shelf-margin wedge from the basin-floor fan
lowstand systems tract from the transgressive systems tract
highstand systems tract from the overlying sequence boundary
transgressive systems tract from the highstand systems tract
cards.e: It marks the furthest landward reach of the sea, at the end of transgression and start of highstand. The surface between lowstand and transgressive tracts is the transgressive surface.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The oldest supracrustal unit of the Dharwar craton, found as high-grade enclaves within the Peninsular Gneiss, is the
cards.e: The Sargur Group is older than 3.0 Ga. The Bababudan Group is the lowest part of the younger Dharwar Supergroup, which rests on the gneiss.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Calicut Univ B.Sc. Geology 'Indian Geology' Nov 2018
cards.q: The Dharwar Supergroup is divided into which two groups?
cards.e: Bababudan is the lower and Chitradurga the upper group. Papaghni-Chitravati belong to the Cuddapah, Alwar-Ajabgarh to the Delhi and Chandarpur-Raipur to the Chhattisgarh Supergroup.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Which statement about the Closepet Granite is correct?
o: It is a Cretaceous granite intruding the Deccan Traps
It is a Neoproterozoic granite marking the end of the Delhi orogeny
It is a Neoarchean (about 2.5 Ga) potassium-rich granite belt trending north-south in Karnataka
It is the 3.3 Ga basement batholith of the Singhbhum craton
cards.e: The Closepet Granite cuts the Dharwar craton as a long N-S belt at about 2.5 Ga. The granite that closes the Delhi orogeny is the Erinpura Granite of Rajasthan.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Calicut Univ M.Sc. Applied Geology 'Stratigraphy and Indian Geology' Nov 2024
cards.q: The Kolar and Hutti gold-bearing schist belts lie in the
cards.e: The eastern block has narrow, volcanic-rich, gold-bearing belts among younger granites. The western block has wide belts richer in sediments and iron-manganese ores.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The Eparchaean Unconformity exposed at Tirumala (Tirupati) separates
o: Dharwar schist below from Kaladgi sandstone above
Gondwana beds below from Rajahmundry sandstone above
Vindhyan sandstone below from Deccan Traps above
Archean granite below from Cuddapah Supergroup quartzite above
cards.e: At Tirumala, Proterozoic Cuddapah quartzite rests on eroded Archean granite. The name means 'after the Archean' and marks a very long break in time.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
Calicut Univ M.Sc. Applied Geology 'Stratigraphy and Indian Geology' Nov 2024
cards.q: Which is the correct upward (oldest to youngest) order of groups in the Vindhyan Supergroup?
cards.e: Hook: S-K-R-B (Semri, Kaimur, Rewa, Bhander). Semri is the Lower Vindhyan and Bhander the youngest; the reversed list is the common trap.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Calicut Univ B.Sc. Geology 'Indian Geology' Nov 2018
cards.q: The lowermost group of the Cuddapah Supergroup is the
cards.e: The order upward is Papaghni, Chitravati, Nallamalai. The Kurnool Group is a separate, younger unit lying unconformably on top.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Calicut Univ B.Sc. Geology 'Indian Geology' Nov 2018
cards.q: Mangampeta in the Cuddapah basin of Andhra Pradesh is famous for one of the world's largest deposits of
cards.e: Mangampeta has bedded baryte in shales of the Nallamalai Group. Chromite is the tempting wrong choice but it comes from ultramafic rocks such as Sukinda and Nuggihalli.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The diamond-bearing Banganapalle Quartzite is the basal formation of the
cards.e: The Kurnool Group starts with the Banganapalle Quartzite, followed by the Narji Limestone. The Papaghni Group starts with the Gulcheru Quartzite instead.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Khondalite is essentially a
o: spessartine garnet-quartz rock rich in manganese
cards.e: Khondalite is a metamorphosed clay-rich sediment with garnet, sillimanite and graphite. Hypersthene granite is charnockite, and the manganese garnet-quartz rock is gondite.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The Achankovil shear zone of south Kerala separates the
o: Madurai Block from the Trivandrum Block (Kerala Khondalite Belt)
Western Dharwar craton from the Eastern Dharwar craton
Dharwar craton from the Nilgiri Block
Bastar craton from the Eastern Ghats Mobile Belt
cards.e: The Kerala Khondalite Belt lies south of the Achankovil shear zone and the Madurai Block north of it. The Dharwar-Nilgiri boundary is the Moyar shear zone.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The Jaduguda uranium deposit and the Mosabani-Rakha copper deposits are located along the
cards.e: All lie on the arcuate Singhbhum Shear Zone (copper belt) of Jharkhand. The Great Boundary Fault is in Rajasthan, between the Aravalli rocks and the Vindhyan basin.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Calicut Univ B.Sc. Geology 'Indian Geology' Nov 2018
cards.q: Which Precambrian unit is correctly matched with its main economic mineral?
cards.e: The Sausar Group of Maharashtra-Madhya Pradesh carries manganese ore with gondite. The Vindhyan gives limestone, sandstone and diamonds, not chromite.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Giant quartz reefs trending NE-SW and mafic dyke swarms trending NW-SE are characteristic of the
cards.e: The Bundelkhand granite massif is cut by long quartz reefs that stand as ridges. Singhbhum is known instead for its Newer Dolerite dykes and iron ore basins.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The stromatolitic rock phosphate deposit of Jhamarkotra near Udaipur occurs in the
cards.e: Jhamarkotra phosphorite lies in dolomite of the Aravalli Supergroup. The Delhi Supergroup is the tempting wrong choice; it hosts the Khetri copper belt.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Calicut Univ B.Sc. Geology 'Indian Geology' Nov 2018
cards.q: The Neoproterozoic (about 750 Ma) rhyolite-dominated volcanic province around Jodhpur in western Rajasthan is the
cards.e: Malani is India's largest felsic volcanic province and is younger than the Erinpura Granite. Bijli Rhyolite is also felsic but belongs to the Dongargarh Supergroup of the Bastar craton.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: UPSC Geologist Exam 2019 Geology Paper I (descriptive)
cards.q: In the Singhbhum craton, which unit is the oldest?
cards.e: The Older Metamorphic Group (about 3.5 Ga) comes first and is intruded by tonalite gneiss and the Singhbhum Granite. The Kolhan Group is the youngest sedimentary cover.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Calicut Univ B.Sc. Geology 'Indian Geology' Nov 2018
cards.q: The Majhgawan diamond-bearing pipe near Panna, Madhya Pradesh, intrudes rocks of the
cards.e: The Majhgawan pipe cuts Kaimur sandstone of the Vindhyan Supergroup. The Cuddapah region also has diamonds, but its pipes are at Wajrakarur, west of the basin.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: In the GSI classification of Kerala's Precambrian rocks, the Vengad Group of Kannur district is regarded as the equivalent of the
cards.e: The Vengad Group (conglomerate, quartzite, mica schist) is equated with the Dharwar Supergroup. The Sargur equivalent in Kerala is the older Wayanad Group.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: 'Incipient' (arrested) charnockite, formed as patches in gneiss by CO2-rich fluids, is classically seen in the Kerala Khondalite Belt at
cards.e: Quarries at Ponmudi near Thiruvananthapuram show dark charnockite patches growing in garnet-biotite gneiss. Ambalavayal is known for a granite, and Varkala for Cenozoic sediments.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
p: Kerala University M.Sc. Geology model questions (GL 231)
cards.q: Pick the odd one out: which of these is a mobile belt and not an Archean craton?
cards.e: The Eastern Ghats is a Proterozoic granulite mobile belt along the east coast. Bastar, Singhbhum and Bundelkhand are stable Archean cratons.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: The Chandarpur Group and the Raipur Group are subdivisions of the
cards.e: Chandarpur (sandy, lower) and Raipur (limestone-shale, upper) make up the Chhattisgarh Supergroup on the Bastar craton. The Kaladgi Supergroup has the Bagalkot and Badami groups.

cards.s: Stratigraphy: Principles, Dating and Precambrian of India
cards.q: Charnockite was named by T. H. Holland after
o: the Charnia fossil of the Ediacaran
a village in the Nilgiri hills
Job Charnock, whose tombstone is made of the rock
cards.e: Holland named it after Job Charnock, founder of Calcutta; the type area is near Chennai. The Khond tribe gave its name to khondalite, named by T. L. Walker.

cards.q: Which pair of properties makes a fossil species most useful as an index (zone) fossil?
o: Short time range and narrow geographic spread
Long time range and wide geographic spread
Short time range and wide geographic spread
Long time range and narrow geographic spread
cards.e: A short life span fixes the age closely, and a wide spread lets distant sections be matched. A long-ranging fossil, however widespread, cannot tell one age from another.

cards.q: Which one of the following is NOT a trace fossil?
cards.e: An internal mould (steinkern) copies the shape of the body itself, so it is a body fossil. Coprolites (fossil dung), footprints and burrows record what the animal did, so they are trace fossils.

cards.q: Leaves in shale and graptolites in black slate are usually preserved as thin black films. This mode of preservation is called:
cards.e: In carbonisation the volatile parts are driven off and only a carbon film stays. Permineralisation is different: minerals fill pore spaces, as in petrified wood.

cards.q: The largest mass extinction in Earth history, which ended the trilobites and the rugose and tabulate corals, took place at the end of the:
cards.e: The end-Permian event (about 252 million years ago) wiped out most marine species and closes the Palaeozoic. The end-Cretaceous event is more famous but smaller, and trilobites were already gone by then.

cards.q: Which of these groups died out completely at the end of the Cretaceous?
cards.e: Ammonites vanish at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary along with belemnites and rudists. Nautiloids look similar but survived, and Nautilus lives today.

cards.q: Which pairing of an animal or plant group with its time of first appearance is correct?
cards.e: The first mammals appear in the Triassic, at about the same time as the first dinosaurs. Reptiles start in the Carboniferous, birds in the Jurassic and flowering plants in the Early Cretaceous.

cards.q: Archaeopteryx, the classic link between reptiles and birds, comes from the:
cards.e: The very fine-grained Solnhofen Limestone preserved even the feather impressions. The Burgess Shale is famous for soft-bodied Cambrian animals, not birds.

cards.q: Two volcanic ash beds dated 80 Ma (lower) and 78 Ma (upper) bracket 20 m of shale laid down at a steady rate. An index fossil is last seen 5 m above the lower ash. Its extinction age is about:
cards.e: 20 m in 2 million years is 10 m per million years. So 5 m took 0.5 million years, giving 80 - 0.5 = 79.5 Ma. The age must fall between the two ash dates, which rules out 77.5 Ma.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Which morphological feature is correctly matched with its fossil group?
cards.e: The pallial sinus is the notch in the mantle line of a burrowing bivalve. The pedicle foramen belongs to brachiopods, the siphuncle to cephalopods and the pygidium (tail shield) to trilobites.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Triassic ammonoids typically show a ceratitic suture. In this pattern:
o: lobes and saddles are all finely frilled
lobes are frilled but saddles are smooth
lobes and saddles are simple and unfrilled
lobes are smooth but saddles are frilled
cards.e: Ceratitic = toothed (frilled) lobes with smooth rounded saddles. Fully frilled lobes and saddles make the ammonitic suture of the Jurassic and Cretaceous; fully simple ones make the goniatitic suture.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: A limestone yields ammonoids with simple zigzag (goniatitic) sutures. Its most likely age is:
cards.e: Goniatites lived from the Devonian to the Permian. Jurassic and Cretaceous ammonoids have complex ammonitic sutures, and no ammonoids survived into the Eocene.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: In a typical brachiopod the plane of symmetry:
o: lies between the two valves, along the commissure
runs parallel to the hinge line through the beak only
passes through the beaks and cuts each valve into equal left and right halves
is absent because the shell is spirally coiled
cards.e: Each brachiopod valve has matching left and right halves, but the two valves differ in size. The plane lying between the valves is the bivalve condition.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: A fossil bivalve shows a deep pallial sinus. This tells us that the animal:
o: burrowed deeply and had long siphons
was cemented to a hard sea floor
cards.e: The sinus is the space into which the siphons were pulled back, so a deep sinus means long siphons and deep burrowing. Cemented forms like oysters have no sinus.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Which of these gastropod genera has a sinistral (left-handed) shell and is typical of the Deccan Inter-trappean beds?
cards.e: Physa is a freshwater snail that coils to the left; Physa prinsepii marks the Inter-trappean lake beds. Turritella, Conus and Natica are normal dextral marine snails.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: The name 'trilobite' refers to the division of the body into:
o: an axial lobe and two pleural lobes
cards.e: The three lobes run lengthwise: a raised central axis with a pleural lobe on each side. Cephalon-thorax-pygidium is the crosswise (head to tail) division and is the common wrong answer.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Which graptolite has a single stipe with thecae on one side only and is typical of the Silurian?
cards.e: Graptolites reduced their branches with time: many (Dictyonema), four (Tetragraptus), two (Didymograptus), one (Monograptus). The two-stiped Didymograptus is Ordovician.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Which of the following is an irregular echinoid?
cards.e: Micraster is a heart-shaped burrowing urchin with bilateral symmetry and the anus outside the apical disc. Cidaris, Echinus and Hemicidaris are regular, round, five-rayed forms.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Corals with septa inserted in multiples of six, ranging from the Triassic to the present day, belong to the:
cards.e: Scleractinians (hexacorals) are the modern reef builders. Rugose corals add septa in fours and, like the tabulate corals, died out at the end of the Permian.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: A porcelaneous test - calcareous, without pores, milky white in reflected light - is characteristic of the:
cards.e: Miliolids build the porcelaneous wall. Fusulinids have a microgranular wall, globigerinids a glassy perforate (hyaline) wall and textulariids an agglutinated wall of cemented grains.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Fusulinid foraminifera are reliable index fossils for the:
cards.e: These wheat-grain shaped larger forams appear in the Carboniferous and die out in the end-Permian extinction. The Eocene-Oligocene larger foram is Nummulites.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Nummulites, the coin-shaped larger foraminifer of the limestones of Kutch, Subathu and Meghalaya, was most abundant in the:
cards.e: Nummulites ranges from Paleocene to Oligocene with its peak in the Eocene. Permian larger forams are fusulinids, and the Late Cretaceous ones include Orbitoides.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Dissepiments and tabulae are skeletal structures found in:
cards.e: Tabulae are horizontal floors and dissepiments are small curved plates inside a coral skeleton. Brachiopods have a delthyrium, echinoids have ambulacra and trilobites have a pygidium.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Which statement about invertebrate fossil morphology is correct?
o: In ammonoids the siphuncle runs along the outer (ventral) margin of the whorl
cards.e: The ammonoid siphuncle is marginal, while in Nautilus it is central. The pallial sinus belongs to bivalves, the glabella to trilobites and the lophophore to brachiopods.

cards.t: Morphology and time-ranges of fossil groups
cards.q: Many foraminifera occur in two forms. The microspheric form has:
o: a siliceous instead of a calcareous test
a large first chamber and a small test
a small first chamber and a large test
cards.e: Microspheric = tiny proloculus (first chamber) but large adult test; megalospheric is the reverse. The two forms come from alternating sexual and asexual generations.

cards.t: Evolutionary changes in molluscs and mammals in geological time
cards.q: Which sequence shows the textbook evolution of the horse from oldest to youngest?
cards.e: Hyracotherium (Eohippus) is Eocene, Mesohippus Oligocene, Merychippus Miocene and Equus Pleistocene. The usual trap is swapping the two 'M' genera: Meso comes before Mery.

cards.t: Evolutionary changes in molluscs and mammals in geological time
cards.q: In the textbook horse lineage, the first one-toed horse was:
cards.e: Pliohippus (Pliocene) lost the side toes. Mesohippus, Merychippus and Hipparion all still had three toes.

cards.t: Evolutionary changes in molluscs and mammals in geological time
cards.q: Which of the following is NOT a trend seen in the evolution of the horse?
o: Lengthening of the face and limbs
Reduction in the number of toes
Lowering of the crowns of the cheek teeth
cards.e: The teeth became high-crowned (hypsodont), not lower, to cope with gritty grass. Size increase, toe loss and longer limbs all helped life on open grassland.

cards.t: Evolutionary changes in molluscs and mammals in geological time
cards.q: Moeritherium, the pig-sized animal placed at the base of the textbook elephant lineage, comes from the:
cards.e: Proboscideans began in Africa, and Moeritherium is from the Eocene beds of the Fayum. Siberia is known for the much later woolly mammoth.

cards.t: Evolutionary changes in molluscs and mammals in geological time
cards.q: The famous skeleton 'Lucy', found in Ethiopia in 1974, belongs to:
cards.e: Lucy is a small upright-walking Australopithecus about 3.2 million years old. Homo erectus is the species of Java Man and Peking Man.

cards.t: Evolutionary changes in molluscs and mammals in geological time
cards.q: The 'Narmada Man' hominin skull cap was discovered at:
cards.e: Arun Sonakia of GSI found it in 1982 in Narmada river gravels at Hathnora. Haritalyangar is the Siwalik ape (Ramapithecus) locality, and Bhimbetka is known for rock shelters.

cards.t: Evolutionary changes in molluscs and mammals in geological time
cards.q: The strong Mesozoic rise of deep-burrowing bivalves with siphons is best explained as a response to:
o: a fall in the oxygen content of the atmosphere
cards.e: As crabs, fishes and marine reptiles that break shells became common, living hidden in the sediment became an advantage. Grasslands are a Cenozoic land feature and have nothing to do with sea-floor life.

cards.q: 'A structure lost in the course of evolution is not regained in its original form.' This statement is:
cards.e: Dollo's law is the law of irreversibility of evolution. Cope's rule is about increase in body size, which is the most common mix-up.

cards.q: The steady increase in body size from Eohippus to Equus is a standard example of:
cards.e: Cope's rule says lineages tend to grow larger with time. Dollo's law deals with irreversibility, not size.

cards.q: The idea that species remain almost unchanged for long periods and then change quickly during short speciation events is called:
cards.e: Punctuated equilibrium (Eldredge and Gould, 1972) explains long stasis broken by rapid change. Phyletic gradualism is the opposite view: slow, even change all the time.

cards.q: The forelimb of a human, the wing of a bat and the flipper of a whale are:
cards.e: They share the same bone plan from a common ancestor but do different jobs, so they are homologous. Analogous organs, like bird and insect wings, do the same job but have different origins.

cards.q: Ichthyosaurs (reptiles) and dolphins (mammals) evolved very similar streamlined bodies. This is an example of:
cards.e: Unrelated groups facing the same way of life arrive at the same shape - that is convergence. Adaptive radiation is the reverse: one group spreading into many different shapes and habits.

cards.t: Use of species and genera of foraminifera and echinodermata in biostratigraphic correlation
cards.q: The planktonic foraminifer Globotruncana is a marker of the:
cards.e: Globotruncana, with its keeled chambers, is confined to the Late Cretaceous and dies out at the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary. Globigerina and Globorotalia are the common Cenozoic planktonic genera.

cards.t: Use of species and genera of foraminifera and echinodermata in biostratigraphic correlation
cards.q: Which larger foraminifer would you expect in a Lower Miocene limestone such as those of Kutch or Quilon?
cards.e: Miogypsina is the Miocene marker. Fusulina is Late Palaeozoic, Orbitoides is Late Cretaceous, and Nummulites peaks in the Eocene and is gone by the end of the Oligocene.

cards.t: Use of species and genera of foraminifera and echinodermata in biostratigraphic correlation
cards.q: Micraster, used to zone the Upper Cretaceous Chalk of England and often quoted as a case of gradual evolution, is:
cards.e: Micraster is a burrowing heart-urchin whose shape changes step by step up through the Chalk. The stemless crinoids of the Chalk are Marsupites and Uintacrinus.

cards.t: Use of species and genera of foraminifera and echinodermata in biostratigraphic correlation
cards.q: Planktonic foraminifera are better than benthic foraminifera for long-distance correlation mainly because they:
o: have thicker tests that resist solution
lived only in shallow, warm lagoons
are larger and easier to see
are spread widely by ocean currents and are not tied to one sea-floor facies
cards.e: Floating forms settle over whole ocean basins at the same time, whatever the bottom sediment. Benthic forms follow depth and substrate, so they are better for reading environment than age.

cards.t: Use of species and genera of foraminifera and echinodermata in biostratigraphic correlation
cards.q: The Um Sohryngkew River section of Meghalaya is important because it exposes:
o: the type section of the Siwalik Group
the Precambrian-Cambrian boundary with trace fossils
a marine Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary with a planktonic foraminiferal turnover
cards.e: Cretaceous planktonic forams disappear there at an iridium-rich boundary clay. India's well-known Permian-Triassic boundary section is Guryul Ravine in Kashmir.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: The three-toed horse Hipparion is the characteristic fossil of the:
cards.e: Hipparion enters with the Nagri Formation and marks the Middle Siwalik. The Upper Siwalik is marked instead by the true one-toed horse Equus.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Which fossil assemblage points to the Upper Siwalik (Pinjor) beds?
cards.e: True horse, true elephant and true cattle arrive together in the Upper Siwalik. Listriodon and Giraffokeryx are Lower Siwalik (Chinji) forms.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Ramapithecus, first described from the Siwaliks of Haritalyangar, is now regarded as:
o: the direct ancestor of Homo erectus
a form of Sivapithecus, related to the orangutan
cards.e: Fuller skull finds showed an orangutan-like face, so Ramapithecus was merged with Sivapithecus. The older view that it was the first human ancestor is the tempting wrong answer.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Which of these fossils would NOT be found in the Siwalik Group?
cards.e: Titanosaurus is a dinosaur of the Cretaceous Lameta Beds; the Siwaliks are Miocene to Pleistocene, long after the dinosaurs. Stegodon (elephant relative), Sivatherium (giraffid) and Hipparion (horse) are all Siwalik mammals.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Gangamopteris differs from Glossopteris in that its leaf:
o: has parallel instead of net-like veins
cards.e: The two tongue-shaped leaves both have net veins, but only Glossopteris has a clear midrib. Gangamopteris dominates the older Talchir and Karharbari beds.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Vertebraria, common in the Lower Gondwana coal measures, is the:
o: root-like underground axis of the Glossopteris plant
leaf of an Upper Gondwana cycad-like plant
cards.e: Vertebraria looks like a string of vertebrae and is found joined to Glossopteris plants as their root system. The Upper Gondwana cycad-like leaf is Ptilophyllum.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Which plant fossil is the guide to the Upper Gondwana (for example the Rajmahal beds)?
cards.e: Ptilophyllum, a cycad-like leaf, names the Jurassic to Early Cretaceous flora. Gangamopteris, Glossopteris and Schizoneura all belong to the Permian Lower Gondwana flora.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Dicroidium, a seed fern with forked fronds, is typical of Gondwana beds of which age?
cards.e: Dicroidium replaced Glossopteris across Gondwanaland after the end-Permian extinction. So it marks the Triassic ('Middle Gondwana'), as in the Parsora beds.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Which of the following does NOT belong to the Glossopteris flora?
cards.e: Lepidodendron is a giant club-moss of the Carboniferous coal forests of Europe and North America. The other three are regular members of the Permian Lower Gondwana flora.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Botanically, the Glossopteris plant was a:
cards.e: Its leaves look fern-like, but it bore seeds, so it is a pteridosperm. 'True fern' is the trap, because of the fern-like name ending '-pteris'.

cards.t: Siwalik vertebrate fauna and Gondwana flora
cards.q: Among these Lower Gondwana plant fossil names, which one refers to a seed?
cards.e: Samaropsis is a small winged seed. Dadoxylon is fossil wood, Vertebraria is a root and Schizoneura is a horsetail-like shoot with leaves.

cards.t: Evidence of life in Precambrian times
cards.q: Stromatolites are best described as:
o: laminated structures built by sediment-trapping mats of cyanobacteria
cards.e: Sticky microbial mats trap and bind sediment layer upon layer. They are organo-sedimentary structures, not shells and not purely chemical growths.

cards.t: Evidence of life in Precambrian times
cards.q: Dickinsonia, Spriggina and Charnia are members of the:
o: small shelly fauna of the earliest Cambrian
cards.e: These soft-bodied forms lived in the last part of the Precambrian and are named after the Ediacara Hills of South Australia. The Burgess Shale fauna is Middle Cambrian.

cards.t: Evidence of life in Precambrian times
cards.q: The carbonaceous megafossils Chuaria and Tawuia in India are best known from the:
cards.e: These disc- and sausage-shaped carbon films occur in Proterozoic Vindhyan shales. The other three units are Phanerozoic and carry normal plant and animal fossils.

cards.t: Evidence of life in Precambrian times
cards.q: The base of the Cambrian System is defined by the first appearance of:
cards.e: Treptichnus pedum is a branching burrow that marks the Precambrian-Cambrian boundary. Hindeodus parvus defines a different boundary - the base of the Triassic.

cards.t: Evidence of life in Precambrian times
cards.q: The stromatolite-bearing rock phosphate deposit of Rajasthan is at:
cards.e: At Jhamarkotra near Udaipur the phosphate sits in Proterozoic Aravalli stromatolites. Khetri is a copper belt, and Zawar and Rampura-Agucha are lead-zinc deposits.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: Conodonts are made of:
cards.e: Conodont elements are apatite (calcium phosphate), so they survive the acid used to dissolve limestone. Opaline silica is the material of radiolaria and diatoms.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: Which pair of microfossil groups has skeletons of opaline silica?
cards.e: Radiolaria (animal-like plankton) and diatoms (algae) both build with silica. Forams, ostracods and coccoliths are calcareous, conodonts phosphatic, and spores and dinoflagellate cysts organic-walled.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: Ostracods are:
o: single-celled protists with a chambered test
tiny crustaceans with a two-valved calcareous carapace
cards.e: They are small relatives of shrimps living inside a hinged two-valved shell. The chambered single-celled group is the foraminifera.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: Coal seams of the Gondwana basins are correlated mainly by palynology because spores and pollen:
o: evolve more slowly than any other fossils
are made of silica and resist weathering
are found only in marine limestone
are abundant, tough-walled and widely spread in non-marine sediments
cards.e: River and swamp deposits have few shells but plenty of wind- and water-borne spores and pollen. Their sporopollenin wall is organic, not silica.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: The presence of Miogypsina in the Quilon Limestone of Kerala shows that its age is:
cards.e: Miogypsina is a larger foram of the Early Miocene, and the Quilon beds are placed in the Burdigalian. An Eocene limestone would carry Nummulites instead.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: The Eocene nummulitic limestone of Meghalaya and Assam is the:
cards.e: The Sylhet Limestone of the Jaintia Group is packed with Nummulites, Assilina and Alveolina. Tipam, Girujan and Dupi Tila are younger, mostly river-laid sands and clays.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: Charophyte gyrogonites and ostracods in the Deccan Inter-trappean beds indicate that these beds were deposited in:
cards.e: Charophytes (stoneworts such as Chara) are freshwater algae. The Inter-trappean sediments formed in lakes on the lava surface between eruptions.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: A limestone from the Cauvery basin contains Globotruncana together with the larger foraminifera Orbitoides and Siderolites. It most likely belongs to the:
cards.e: This is a latest Cretaceous (Campanian-Maastrichtian) assemblage, the age of the Ariyalur Group. The Niniyur beds just above are Danian, after Globotruncana died out.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: Which microfossils are the main ingredient of chalk?
cards.e: Chalk is a soft limestone made mostly of coccoliths, the tiny calcite plates of planktonic algae. Radiolaria and diatoms are siliceous and form chert and diatomite instead.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: The colour of conodonts (Conodont Alteration Index) is used to estimate:
o: the absolute age of the rock in years
the depth of water at deposition
the maximum temperature the rock has reached
the salinity of the ancient sea
cards.e: Conodonts darken from pale yellow to black as organic matter in them is heated. This shows the thermal maturity of the rock, which matters for oil and gas.

cards.t: Different microfossil groups and their distribution in India
cards.q: Which region gives the reference sequence for larger foraminiferal zonation of the Indian Tertiary, with Nummulites and Assilina in the Eocene and Miogypsina in the Miocene?
cards.e: The shelf limestones of Kutch (Gujarat) are packed with larger forams of Eocene to Miocene age. The Damodar valley is Gondwana (non-marine), and Cuddapah and Vindhyan are Precambrian basins.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Palaeozoic formations of India
cards.q: Which area of India preserves an almost unbroken marine fossil-bearing sequence from the Cambrian to the Cretaceous?
cards.e: Spiti lay under the Tethys sea for most of the Palaeozoic and Mesozoic, so its record is nearly complete. The Damodar valley has thick beds too, but they are river-laid Gondwana rocks, not marine.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Palaeozoic formations of India
cards.q: The white, nearly unfossiliferous Muth Quartzite of Spiti is assigned mainly to the
cards.e: The Muth Quartzite is Devonian (it may begin in the late Silurian). The Permian of Spiti is the Kuling Group with Productus Shales, a very different dark shaly unit.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Palaeozoic formations of India
cards.q: Which of these Salt Range units is NOT part of the Cambrian succession?
cards.e: The Speckled Sandstone is Permian and lies above the glacial Boulder Bed. Purple Sandstone, Neobolus Shales, Magnesian Sandstone and Salt Pseudomorph Shales make up the Cambrian.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Palaeozoic formations of India
cards.q: In the Salt Range, the glacial Boulder Bed of Talchir age rests directly on rocks of which age?
cards.e: The Ordovician to Middle Carboniferous is missing there, so the Boulder Bed lies straight on the Cambrian. Devonian and Lower Carboniferous beds were never laid down in the Salt Range.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Palaeozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Syringothyris Limestone of Kashmir is of which age?
cards.e: It is Lower Carboniferous, named after the brachiopod Syringothyris, and is followed by the Middle Carboniferous Fenestella Shales. The Upper Permian of Kashmir is the Zewan beds.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Palaeozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Panjal Trap lava flows of Kashmir were erupted mainly during the
cards.e: The Panjal Volcanics (Agglomeratic Slate and Panjal Trap) are Late Carboniferous to Permian. Late Cretaceous is the age of the Deccan Traps, the usual wrong pick.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Palaeozoic formations of India
cards.q: In Kashmir, plant beds with Gangamopteris are overlain by marine beds that fix a Permian age for the Lower Gondwana flora. These marine beds are the
cards.e: The Upper Permian marine Zewan beds lie on the Gangamopteris beds. Subathu beds are Eocene and Karewas are Plio-Pleistocene, far too young.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: The ammonoid-rich Triassic rocks of Spiti are grouped as the
cards.e: Lilang is the Triassic of Spiti. Haimanta is Cambrian, Kanawar is Carboniferous and Kuling is Permian, so all three are Palaeozoic.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: In Spiti, the zone of Otoceras woodwardi marks the
cards.e: The Otoceras zone is the lowest Triassic zone, lying right on the Permian Productus Shales. It is therefore the Permian-Triassic boundary marker in Spiti.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: 'Saligrams' are ammonite-bearing concretions found in the
cards.e: Saligrams come from the black Upper Jurassic Spiti Shales. Productus Shales are Permian and carry brachiopods, not these ammonite nodules.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Which is the correct order of the Jurassic series of Kutch, from oldest to youngest?
cards.e: Patcham (Bathonian) is the oldest and Umia the youngest, reaching the Lower Cretaceous. Hook: 'Please Come Kutch, Uncle'.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Dhosa Oolite, a widely traced ammonite-rich marker bed of Kutch, lies at the top of the
cards.e: The Dhosa Oolite (Oxfordian) caps the Chari Series. The Katrol Series lies just above it, which makes it the tempting wrong choice.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Which Kutch unit carries Upper Gondwana plants such as Ptilophyllum interbedded with marine ammonite-bearing beds?
cards.e: The Umia plant beds hold the Ptilophyllum flora, and the marine layers with them give a latest Jurassic to Lower Cretaceous date. The Patcham is fully marine limestone and shale.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Arrange the Cretaceous units of the Trichinopoly area from oldest to youngest.
cards.e: The order is Uttatur, Trichinopoly, Ariyalur, Niniyur (hook U-T-A-N). Niniyur is the youngest and is actually Danian, just above the Cretaceous.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Niniyur beds, which lack ammonites and carry Nautilus danicus, are of which age?
cards.e: They are Danian (earliest Paleocene). Ammonites died out at the end of the Maastrichtian, so beds without them above the Ariyalur are post-Cretaceous.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Nimar Sandstone, Nodular Limestone and Coralline Limestone together make up the
cards.e: These three are the Bagh Beds of the lower Narmada valley, a marine Cretaceous unit. The Lameta Beds are also in the Narmada region but are river and lake deposits with dinosaurs.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Which statement about Cretaceous marine faunas of India is correct?
o: Neither area has marine fossils, as the beds in each are river deposits
Bagh Bed fossils are Indo-Pacific, while Trichinopoly fossils are of European type
Bagh and Trichinopoly fossils are identical, proving one open sea across the Peninsula
Bagh Bed fossils have Arabian-European affinity, while Trichinopoly fossils are of Indo-Pacific type
cards.e: The Bagh sea was an arm of the western (Tethyan) sea and the Trichinopoly sea belonged to the Indo-Pacific. The difference shows a land barrier lay between them.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Lameta Beds are best described as
o: Eocene nummulitic limestones lying above the Deccan Traps
Permian glacial boulder beds at the base of the Gondwana
Maastrichtian river and lake deposits with dinosaur remains, lying below the Deccan Traps
cards.e: The Lameta Beds are infra-trappean, latest Cretaceous, freshwater deposits with dinosaur bones and eggs. Marine Cenomanian limestones describe the Bagh Beds instead.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Which statement about the Deccan Traps is correct?
o: They are fissure-fed tholeiitic flood basalts erupted around the Cretaceous-Paleogene boundary
They are rhyolite ash flows of Permian age
They are submarine pillow lavas erupted in the Jurassic
They are andesite lavas from central volcanoes of Miocene age
cards.e: The Deccan Traps are flood basalts poured out of long fissures about 66 million years ago, mostly on land. They are not central-volcano andesites.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: The freshwater snail Physa prinsepii is the characteristic fossil of the
cards.e: Inter-trappean beds are lake sediments between lava flows, and Physa prinsepii is their typical fossil. The Quilon Limestone is marine and the Talchir bed is glacial.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Sedimentary beds that lie beneath the lowest Deccan lava flow, such as the Lameta Beds, are called
cards.e: Infra means below, so infra-trappean beds lie under the whole lava pile. Inter-trappean beds lie between two flows.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Mesozoic formations of India
cards.q: Deccan Trap volcanism is linked to the passage of India over which hotspot?
cards.e: India passed over the Reunion hotspot at about 66 million years ago. Kerguelen is linked to the older Rajmahal Traps, so it is the common trap answer.

cards.q: Who gave the name 'Gondwana' to the plant-bearing continental rocks of central India?
cards.e: Medlicott used the name in 1872 after the Gond kingdom. Suess later borrowed it for the supercontinent Gondwanaland, so he is the tempting wrong answer.

cards.q: The Gondwana Supergroup of India ranges in age from
cards.e: It begins with the Permo-Carboniferous Talchir glacial beds and ends in the Lower Cretaceous with units like the Rajmahal and Jabalpur. It is neither older Palaeozoic nor Tertiary.

cards.q: Striated and faceted boulders set in fine clay, overlain by varved shales, are typical of which Gondwana unit?
cards.e: These are glacial features and mark the Talchir Formation at the base of the Gondwana. The Barakar above is a coal-bearing river and swamp deposit.

cards.q: Odd one out: which formation does NOT belong to the Damuda Group?
cards.e: The Damuda Group is Barakar, Barren Measures and Raniganj, all Permian. The Panchet is Lower Triassic and lies above the Damuda.

cards.q: Most of India's coal, including the prime coking coal of Jharia, comes from the
cards.e: The Lower Permian Barakar Formation is the chief coal-bearing unit. The Talchir is glacial and the Panchet is a coal-free red-bed unit.

cards.q: The 'Ironstone Shales' of the Raniganj coalfield are the local name for the
cards.e: The Barren Measures, between the Barakar and Raniganj formations, have no workable coal but carry clay-ironstone nodules. The Karharbari lies lower down and does carry coal.

cards.q: A Lower Triassic unit of red and chocolate clays, without coal, that yields the reptile Lystrosaurus is the
cards.e: The Panchet Formation is the red, coal-free Lower Triassic unit with Lystrosaurus. The Raniganj below it is Upper Permian and coal-bearing.

cards.q: Pachmarhi, Denwa and Bagra formations make up which group, and in which basin?
cards.e: They form the Mahadeva Group of the Satpura basin in Madhya Pradesh. The Damuda Group is the Permian coal-bearing group of the Damodar valley.

cards.q: The Kota Formation, with a fish-bearing limestone band and the dinosaur Barapasaurus, belongs to which basin and age?
cards.e: The Kota is the Lower Jurassic unit of the Pranhita-Godavari basin, above the Maleri and Dharmaram formations. It is not part of the Damodar sequence.

cards.q: Which pairing of Gondwana division and its characteristic flora is correct?
o: Lower Gondwana - Glossopteris flora; Upper Gondwana - Ptilophyllum flora
Lower Gondwana - Lepidodendron flora; Upper Gondwana - Glossopteris flora
Lower Gondwana - Glossopteris flora; Upper Gondwana - Lepidodendron flora
Lower Gondwana - Ptilophyllum flora; Upper Gondwana - Glossopteris flora
cards.e: Glossopteris marks the Permian Lower Gondwana and Ptilophyllum the Jurassic-Cretaceous Upper Gondwana. Lepidodendron belongs to the northern coal forests, not to Gondwana.

cards.q: Red beds without coal in the Panchet and Mahadeva units point to which climate?
cards.e: Red colour (oxidised iron) and no coal show a dry climate in the Triassic. Glacial conditions belong only to the Talchir at the base.

cards.q: Compared with the Tertiary coal of Assam, Gondwana coal of India is typically
o: low in ash and low in sulphur
low in ash and high in sulphur
high in ash and high in sulphur
high in ash and low in sulphur
cards.e: Gondwana coal is of drift origin, so it is high in ash, but it is low in sulphur. Assam Tertiary coal is the reverse: low ash, high sulphur.

cards.q: The Singareni coalfield, the only major coalfield of South India, lies in which Gondwana basin?
cards.e: Singareni is in the Godavari valley of Telangana. Jharia, Bokaro and Raniganj lie in the Damodar valley far to the north-east.

cards.q: The South African glacial unit that matches the Talchir boulder bed of India is the
cards.e: The Dwyka tillite at the base of the Karoo matches the Talchir. The Ecca beds above it are coal measures and match the Damuda.

cards.q: Which landmass was NOT a part of Gondwanaland?
cards.e: North America belonged to the northern supercontinent Laurasia. Gondwanaland was South America, Africa, Madagascar, India, Australia and Antarctica.

cards.q: Which of these is an Upper Gondwana unit exposed on the east coast of India?
cards.e: The Athgarh Sandstone near Cuttack is an east-coast Upper Gondwana unit. Nimar Sandstone is part of the marine Bagh Beds and Tipam Sandstone is Miocene of Assam.

cards.q: Which Upper Gondwana unit consists of basalt flows with plant-bearing sedimentary layers between them?
cards.e: The Rajmahal Formation is a pile of Lower Cretaceous lava flows with inter-trappean plant beds. The Jabalpur Formation is Upper Gondwana too, but it is clay and sandstone without lavas.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: In the Tertiary of Assam, the coal-bearing group of Oligocene age is the
cards.e: The Barail Group holds the Makum coal of Upper Assam. The Jaintia Group is Eocene and known for the nummulitic Sylhet Limestone.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: The main oil reservoir of the Digboi field in Assam is the
cards.e: Digboi oil comes from the Miocene Tipam Sandstone. The Girujan Clay lies above it and acts as the seal (cap rock), not the reservoir.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: The last marine deposit in the Sub-Himalaya of Himachal Pradesh, a nummulite-bearing unit of Paleocene-Eocene age, is the
cards.e: The Subathu is marine and nummulitic. The Dagshai and Kasauli above it are river deposits, showing that the sea had withdrawn.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: In the Jammu foothills, which continental red-bed unit lies directly below the Siwalik Group?
cards.e: The Murree Group (Oligocene to Lower Miocene) underlies the Siwaliks. The Subathu is older still and marine, lying below the Murree.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Neyveli lignite of Tamil Nadu occurs in the
cards.e: The lignite lies in the Mio-Pliocene Cuddalore Sandstone. The Ariyalur Group is Cretaceous marine rock of the same region and has no lignite.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: Which is the correct order of the Tertiary formations of Kerala, from oldest to youngest?
cards.e: Vaikom is at the base, the marine Quilon in the middle and Warkalli on top (V-Q-W). Laterite usually caps the Warkalli.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Quilon Formation of Kerala, typically seen at Padappakkara near Kollam, is best described as
o: a Cretaceous coral-reef limestone with ammonites
a Lower Miocene marine fossil-rich limestone with marl and clay
a Pliocene river gravel with lignite
cards.e: It is a Lower Miocene marine limestone unit, rich in corals, molluscs and foraminifera. Lignite-bearing sands and clays describe the Warkalli beds above it.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: Sandstone and variegated clay with carbonaceous clay, lignite seams and marcasite, exposed in the sea cliff at Varkala, belong to the
cards.e: The Varkala cliff is the type section of the Mio-Pliocene Warkalli Formation. The Cuddalore Formation is its equivalent in Tamil Nadu, not a Kerala unit.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: In coastal Kerala, the principal confined aquifers are found in the
o: limestone and clay of the Quilon Formation
sands of the Warkalli and Vaikom formations
cards.e: The sandy Warkalli and Vaikom beds store and yield water under pressure. The Quilon unit is mostly clay and marl and is a poor aquifer; Kerala has no Deccan Trap.

cards.t: Rise of the Himalaya and evolution of Siwalik basin
cards.q: Which thrust separates the Lesser Himalaya from the Higher (Great) Himalaya?
cards.e: The Main Central Thrust carries Higher Himalayan crystalline rocks over the Lesser Himalaya. The Main Boundary Thrust lies further south, between the Lesser Himalaya and the Siwaliks.

cards.t: Rise of the Himalaya and evolution of Siwalik basin
cards.q: Going from the Ganga plain northward, in what order are the major Himalayan thrusts crossed?
cards.e: First the Himalayan Frontal Thrust, then the Main Boundary Thrust, then the Main Central Thrust. They also get older in the same direction.

cards.t: Rise of the Himalaya and evolution of Siwalik basin
cards.q: Ophiolites and melange marking the line where India joined Asia occur along the
cards.e: A suture is the scar of a closed ocean, and ophiolites are slices of that ocean floor. The three thrusts all lie within the Indian plate, south of the suture.

cards.t: Rise of the Himalaya and evolution of Siwalik basin
cards.q: According to the classical account (Wadia), the most powerful phase of Himalayan uplift took place in the
cards.e: The Middle Miocene phase was the strongest, after an earlier end-Eocene phase. A later Plio-Pleistocene phase folded the Siwaliks.

cards.t: Rise of the Himalaya and evolution of Siwalik basin
cards.q: The Kamlial and Chinji formations belong to the
cards.e: Kamlial and Chinji make up the Lower Siwalik. Nagri and Dhok Pathan are Middle Siwalik; Tatrot, Pinjor and Boulder Conglomerate are Upper Siwalik.

cards.t: Rise of the Himalaya and evolution of Siwalik basin
cards.q: The Siwalik Group is best described as
o: shallow-marine shelf limestone laid on a passive margin
deep-marine flysch laid in an ocean trench
freshwater molasse laid in a foreland basin
glacial tillite laid by ice sheets
cards.e: Siwalik beds are river-laid debris shed from the rising Himalaya into the trough in front of it, which is called molasse. Flysch is the earlier deep-sea deposit, the usual confusion.

cards.t: Rise of the Himalaya and evolution of Siwalik basin
cards.q: Which unit forms the top of the Upper Siwalik and records the final strong uplift of the Himalaya?
cards.e: The Siwaliks coarsen upward and end in the Boulder Conglomerate. Chinji is near the base and is mostly red mudstone.

cards.q: The Karewas of Kashmir are
o: Permian basalt flows of the Pir Panjal
Plio-Pleistocene lake and river deposits forming flat terraces
cards.e: Karewas were laid in a large lake that once filled the Kashmir valley. Permian basalt flows of the Pir Panjal are the Panjal Traps.

cards.q: In the Indo-Gangetic plain, the older alluvium that lies above flood level and contains kankar nodules is called
cards.e: Bhangar is the older (Pleistocene) alluvium with kankar. Khadar is the newer flood-plain alluvium that is renewed each year.

cards.q: The porous gravel belt along the foot of the Siwalik hills, where streams disappear underground, is the
cards.e: Bhabar is the coarse gravel zone at the hill foot. Terai is the marshy belt south of it where the lost water seeps out again.

cards.q: The term 'laterite' was first used by Francis Buchanan in 1807 for a rock seen at
cards.e: Buchanan named laterite at Angadipuram in Kerala. Varkala is famous for the Warkalli cliff section, which is capped by laterite but is not the naming site.

cards.q: The base of the Quaternary, as ratified by IUGS in 2009, is placed at about
cards.e: The Quaternary starts at 2.58 million years, the base of the Gelasian Stage. 11,700 years is the start of the Holocene, not of the Quaternary.

cards.q: The Meghalayan Age (ratified 2018), the youngest division of the Holocene, began about
cards.e: It began 4,200 years ago, defined in a stalagmite from Mawmluh Cave, Meghalaya. 8,200 years is the start of the Northgrippian and 11,700 years the start of the Greenlandian.

cards.q: Using the ratified boundaries (Quaternary base 2.58 million years, Holocene base 11,700 years), about how long did the Pleistocene Epoch last?
cards.e: 2,580,000 minus 11,700 is about 2,568,000 years, or roughly 2.57 million years. The Pleistocene is almost the whole Quaternary; the Holocene is only its last sliver.

cards.q: Which statement about the Quaternary of Kerala is correct?
o: The Chavara heavy-mineral sands are of Cretaceous marine origin
Laterite in Kerala is found only on Deccan Trap basalt
Kerala's coastal plain is built of Gondwana coal measures
Laterite caps the crystalline rocks of the midlands as well as the Tertiary Warkalli beds
cards.e: Laterite formed on old crystalline rocks and on the young Warkalli beds alike, so weathering continued into the Quaternary. Kerala has no Deccan Trap or Gondwana rocks, and the Chavara sands are Quaternary beach placers.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: Among the Tertiary units of coastal Kerala, which one is the most widely tapped (most extensively developed) aquifer system, as per CGWB?
cards.e: The sandy Warkalli beds are the most widely tapped Tertiary aquifer in Kerala. The Vaikom beds are also good aquifers but lie deeper and are less developed; the Quilon beds are mostly clay and limestone.

cards.t: Stratigraphy of the Cenozoic formations of India
cards.q: The Warkalli Formation of Kerala is a part of the
cards.e: The Warkalli beds are Mio-Pliocene sands and clays, the top unit of Kerala's Tertiary sequence. Khondalite is the old crystalline basement on which these sediments rest.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: How many crystal classes (point groups) are possible in crystals?
cards.e: There are 32 crystal classes. The other numbers belong to the same family and are easy to mix up: 7 crystal systems, 14 Bravais lattices and 230 space groups.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which rotation axis of symmetry can never occur in a crystal?
cards.e: A repeating lattice allows only 2-, 3-, 4- and 6-fold axes. Five-fold units cannot fill space without gaps, just as pentagon tiles cannot cover a floor. The 6-fold axis is real: beryl and apatite have it.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: The galena-type (normal) class of the cubic system has how many axes of symmetry in all?
cards.e: It has three 4-fold, four 3-fold and six 2-fold axes: 3 + 4 + 6 = 13. Nine is the number of planes, and 23 is the total of all elements (9 planes + 13 axes + 1 centre).

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: A crystal has three unequal axes; two of the angles between them are 90° and the third (beta) is not. It belongs to which system?
cards.e: One oblique angle with three unequal axes defines the monoclinic system. Orthorhombic also has three unequal axes, but there all three angles are 90°. In triclinic no angle is 90°.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: A crystal shows three mutually perpendicular 2-fold axes, three planes of symmetry and a centre, but no axis higher than 2-fold. Its crystal system is
cards.e: Three 2-fold axes at right angles is the mark of the orthorhombic system (barite type). Monoclinic has only one 2-fold axis and one plane. Tetragonal must have a 4-fold axis.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which mineral is correctly matched with its crystal system?
cards.e: Zircon is tetragonal. Kyanite is triclinic, olivine is orthorhombic and gypsum is monoclinic. Kyanite is the easy trap because its partner sillimanite is orthorhombic.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Three of these minerals crystallise in the cubic system. Which one is the odd one out?
cards.e: Beryl is hexagonal and forms six-sided prisms. Galena, garnet and fluorite are all cubic. Fluorite may tempt because its cleavage is octahedral, but an octahedron is itself a cubic form.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: A crystal face cuts the axes at 2a, 3b and 6c. Its Miller indices are
cards.e: Take reciprocals of the intercepts: 1/2, 1/3, 1/6. Multiply by 6 to clear fractions: 3, 2, 1, so the face is (321). Writing the intercepts directly as (236) is the common mistake.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: In the cubic system, the form {100}, in which every face cuts one axis and is parallel to the other two, is the
cards.e: The cube has six such faces. An octahedron face {111} cuts all three axes equally, and a rhombic dodecahedron face {110} cuts two axes and is parallel to one.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: How many faces does a trisoctahedron have?
cards.e: A trisoctahedron is an octahedron with each face replaced by three faces: 8 x 3 = 24. Eight is the plain octahedron, and 48 belongs to the hexoctahedron.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: In the normal class of the tetragonal system, the form {001} is made of two parallel faces that cut only the c axis. It is called the
cards.e: A pinacoid is an open form of two parallel faces; on {001} it is the basal pinacoid. A pedion is a single face only, and prism faces are parallel to the c axis rather than cutting it.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which of these minerals does NOT crystallise in the cubic system at room temperature, although its crystals look cubic?
cards.e: Leucite forms trapezohedra that look cubic, but at room temperature its structure is tetragonal; it is cubic only at high temperature. Garnet also forms trapezohedra but is truly cubic.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which mineral will scratch apatite but is itself scratched by quartz?
cards.e: Orthoclase has hardness 6, between apatite (5) and quartz (7). Fluorite (4) and calcite (3) are softer than apatite. Topaz (8) is harder than quartz.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which list gives the minerals in correct order of increasing Mohs hardness?
cards.e: Gypsum 2, calcite 3, apatite 5, quartz 7 is in rising order. Each other list has one pair out of order: calcite (3) placed before gypsum (2), fluorite (4) before calcite (3), or apatite (5) before fluorite (4).

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which mineral shows clearly different hardness in different directions: about 5 along its length and about 7 across it?
cards.e: Kyanite blades can be scratched by a knife lengthwise but not crosswise; hence its old name disthene ('two strengths'). Andalusite and sillimanite have the same formula but nearly uniform hardness.

cards.t: Minerals of the carbonate, phosphate, sulphide and halide groups
cards.q: Fluorite commonly grows as cubes. How does it cleave?
cards.e: Fluorite has perfect octahedral cleavage in four directions. Cubic cleavage belongs to halite and galena, dodecahedral to sphalerite and rhombohedral to calcite. Crystal shape and cleavage shape need not match.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: A colourless glassy mineral scratches glass, shows no cleavage and breaks with a shell-like (conchoidal) fracture. It is most likely
cards.e: Quartz (hardness 7) has no cleavage and a conchoidal fracture. Orthoclase also scratches glass but shows two good cleavages. Calcite and fluorite are too soft and cleave perfectly.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which mineral is correctly matched with its streak?
cards.e: Hematite always gives a cherry-red to red-brown streak. Magnetite's streak is black, cinnabar's is scarlet, and pyrite's is greenish black. Pyrite looks golden, but its powder is dark.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Walker's steelyard balance is used to find which property of a mineral?
cards.e: It compares the weight of a mineral in air and in water to give specific gravity; Jolly's spring balance does the same job. Hardness is tested by scratching, not by weighing.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Thin plates of which mineral are used to control frequency in watches and radios because the mineral is piezoelectric?
cards.e: Quartz has no centre of symmetry, so pressure produces electric charge on it. Garnet, orthoclase and calcite all have a centre of symmetry and cannot be piezoelectric.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Forsterite and fayalite have the same crystal structure and show continuous variation in Mg and Fe content. This relationship is an example of
cards.e: Mg2+ and Fe2+ replace each other freely in olivine, so the two end members form a complete solid solution. Polymorphism is the opposite case: same composition but different structures.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which substitution explains the continuous change in composition from albite to anorthite?
o: Ca2+ with Al3+ replaces Na+ with Si4+
cards.e: It is a coupled substitution: Ca2+ comes in for Na+ and, at the same time, Al3+ comes in for Si4+, so charges stay balanced. Ca2+ replacing Na+ alone would leave one extra positive charge.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which of these is NOT a pair of polymorphs?
cards.e: Calcite is CaCO3 and dolomite is CaMg(CO3)2: different compositions, so they are not polymorphs. Each of the other pairs shares one formula (CaCO3, FeS2, C) with two structures.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Perthite is an intergrowth in which
o: a potassium feldspar host contains exsolved lamellae of sodic feldspar
a plagioclase host contains exsolved lamellae of potassium feldspar
quartz and potassium feldspar are intergrown in a wedge-shaped (cuneiform) pattern
worm-like quartz is intergrown with plagioclase
cards.e: Perthite is K-feldspar with unmixed albite strings. The reverse, plagioclase host with K-feldspar lamellae, is antiperthite. The other two are graphic texture and myrmekite.

cards.q: What is the Si:O ratio in the double-chain structure of amphiboles?
cards.e: The amphibole double chain is (Si4O11). The ratio 1:3 belongs to single chains (pyroxenes) and rings, 2:5 to sheets and 2:7 to paired tetrahedra.

cards.q: In the sheet structure of phyllosilicates, how many of its four oxygens does each SiO4 tetrahedron share with its neighbours?
cards.e: Each tetrahedron shares three corners to make a flat sheet, giving Si:O = 2:5. Sharing all four oxygens gives a three-dimensional framework, as in quartz and feldspar.

cards.q: Which silicate class is correctly matched with its example?
cards.e: Beryl has six-member rings of tetrahedra, so it is a cyclosilicate. Epidote is a sorosilicate, tremolite is a double-chain amphibole, and talc is a sheet silicate.

cards.q: Which mineral contains paired tetrahedra, (Si2O7) groups, and is classed as a sorosilicate?
cards.e: Epidote is the commonest sorosilicate; it has Si2O7 pairs along with some single tetrahedra. Olivine has only isolated tetrahedra, beryl has rings and enstatite has single chains.

cards.q: Three of these minerals are framework silicates (tectosilicates). Which is the odd one out?
cards.e: Muscovite is a sheet silicate (phyllosilicate). Quartz, orthoclase and nepheline (a feldspathoid) all have three-dimensional frameworks in which every oxygen is shared.

cards.q: Which statement about silicate structures is correct?
o: Micas have an Si:O ratio of 1:2
In tectosilicates all four oxygens of each tetrahedron are shared
cards.e: Sharing all four oxygens gives the framework of quartz and feldspar. Pyroxenes are single chains (amphiboles are double), micas are sheets with ratio 2:5, and olivine has isolated tetrahedra.

cards.t: Common minerals of igneous and metamorphic rocks
cards.q: Which of these minerals can occur in stable equilibrium with free quartz in an igneous rock?
cards.e: Orthoclase is silica-saturated, so it sits happily beside quartz, as in granite. Forsterite, nepheline and leucite are silica-poor and would react with quartz to form enstatite, albite and K-feldspar.

cards.t: Common minerals of igneous and metamorphic rocks
cards.q: Which garnet is a calcium-chromium silicate with an emerald-green colour?
cards.e: Uvarovite is Ca3Cr2Si3O12; chromium gives the green colour. Grossular (Ca-Al) and andradite (Ca-Fe) are the other calcium garnets. Almandine is the red iron-aluminium garnet of schists.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Two sets of cleavage meeting at about 87° and 93° are characteristic of
cards.e: Pyroxenes have two cleavages at nearly right angles. Amphiboles have two cleavages at 56° and 124°. Micas have only one cleavage and garnets have none.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: A black to dark green prismatic mineral in a diorite shows two cleavages meeting at about 56° and 124° and a six-sided cross-section. It is
cards.e: The 56°/124° cleavage pair is the mark of an amphibole, and hornblende is the common one. Augite, a pyroxene, looks similar but its cleavages meet at about 90°.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Three of these minerals are amphiboles. Which one is the odd one out?
cards.e: Hedenbergite CaFeSi2O6 is a clinopyroxene, the iron partner of diopside. Tremolite (calcic), riebeckite (sodic) and anthophyllite (orthorhombic) are all amphiboles.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which lithium-bearing mineral belongs to the pyroxene group?
cards.e: Spodumene LiAlSi2O6 is the lithium pyroxene of pegmatites. Lepidolite also carries lithium but is a mica, and petalite is a lithium silicate that is not a pyroxene. Jadeite is a sodium pyroxene.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Chrysotile, the main commercial type of asbestos, belongs to which mineral group?
cards.e: Chrysotile is the fibrous form of serpentine, also called white asbestos. Amphibole is the tempting answer because crocidolite and amosite are amphibole asbestos, but they are the less common types.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Black cotton soils swell when wet and crack deeply when dry mainly because they are rich in
cards.e: Montmorillonite (smectite) is a 2:1 clay that takes water between its layers and swells. Kaolinite is a 1:1 clay with tightly bonded layers and does not swell. Illite's layers are locked by potassium.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which clay mineral has a 1:1 layer made of one tetrahedral sheet and one octahedral sheet?
cards.e: Kaolinite is the 1:1 (T-O) clay. Illite, montmorillonite and vermiculite are all 2:1 (T-O-T) clays, with an octahedral sheet between two tetrahedral sheets.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: A plagioclase feldspar contains 62 mol% anorthite. Its name is
cards.e: Labradorite covers An50 to An70, so An62 falls inside it. Andesine is An30-50 and bytownite is An70-90. Labradorite is the usual plagioclase of basalt and gabbro.

cards.t: Common minerals of igneous and metamorphic rocks
cards.q: Clear, glassy potassium feldspar phenocrysts in a rhyolite or trachyte lava are most likely
cards.e: Sanidine is the high-temperature K-feldspar preserved by fast cooling in volcanic rocks. Microcline is the low-temperature form of slowly cooled granites and pegmatites. Anorthite is a calcium plagioclase.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: Which statement about feldspars is correct?
o: Plagioclase feldspars are mainly potassium aluminosilicates
Sanidine is the typical potassium feldspar of slowly cooled granites
Anorthite is the sodium end member of plagioclase
Microcline is the triclinic, low-temperature potassium feldspar
cards.e: Microcline is triclinic and forms at low temperature. Plagioclase is a sodium-calcium series, anorthite is its calcium end member, and sanidine belongs to quickly cooled volcanic rocks.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
cards.q: At 1 atmosphere pressure, low (alpha) quartz changes to high (beta) quartz at about
cards.e: The alpha-beta inversion is at 573 °C. 870 °C is where tridymite becomes stable and 1470 °C is where cristobalite takes over.

cards.t: Common minerals of igneous and metamorphic rocks
cards.q: The presence of which silica polymorph in a rock is taken as evidence of ultra-high-pressure metamorphism or meteorite impact?
cards.e: Coesite is a dense, high-pressure form of SiO2. Tridymite and cristobalite are high-temperature, low-pressure forms found in volcanic rocks, so they point the opposite way.

cards.t: Common minerals of igneous and metamorphic rocks
cards.q: Chiastolite, which shows a dark cross in cross-section, is a variety of
cards.e: Chiastolite is andalusite with carbon-rich inclusions arranged as a cross. Staurolite is the tempting answer, but its 'cross' is made by two twinned crystals, not by inclusions.

cards.t: Physical, chemical and crystallographic characteristics of common rock forming silicate mineral groups
